items.title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
items.abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.

items.title: From Emotion to Expression: The AL–DL–CL Framework for Understanding Communication in the Age of AI and Digital Media
items.abstract: Rapid progress in digital media and artificial intelligence is transforming human communication, facilitating the rapid exchange of messages and minimizing the chances of reflective interpretation. Existing theories in linguistics, psychology, and cultural studies address the structural, cognitive, or social aspects of language, yet fail to explain how emotional processing, internal linguistic structuring, and culturally mediated communication function as a coherent, dynamic system. Through this model, the authors present the AL–DL–CL framework that explores how three layers are engaged in a process that results in communication, through a recursive interaction between the Automatic Layer (AL), the Deliberate Layer (DL), and the Cultural Language Layer (CL). In such a process, the affective or unconscious processes in AL are consistently reframed into structured internal representations via DL, and through CL, and translated back into culturally-expressed language serves as a feedback mechanism, with a tendency to modify cognition and emotional response. Based on a multi-method exploratory approach of sequential cultural transmission, clinical case study analysis, and group-based validation, the results indicate that language is not so much a static container for meaning as a process of reconstruction that is molded by the dynamic interaction between emotion, cognition, and culture. This model also demonstrates how digitally mediated communication can amplify AL-directed reaction and limit DL-level thinking, which increases the potential for misinterpretation, polarization, or misinformation. The AL–DL–CL framework provides guidance in a unified theoretical perspective around language emergence, responsible AI design and digital literacy and intercultural discourse based on the continuous transformation system of communication, and not on the linear encoding.

items.title: Metaphysical Nūr And Generation Alpha: Technology, Ontology, and the Crisis of Orientation
items.abstract: Purpose - This study examines the Islamic metaphysical concept of Nūr (light) as an ontological and epistemic framework for understanding the technological condition of Generation Alpha. The purpose is to clarify the distinction between technological illumination—characterized by visibility, access, and informational abundance—and orienting illumination, understood as intelligibility, guidance, and meaning. By doing so, the paper seeks to address the growing crisis of orientation affecting younger generations in digitally saturated environments. Methods - The research adopts a qualitative, theoretical, and interdisciplinary methodology. It combines hermeneutic analysis of Qurʾānic texts and classical Islamic philosophy with conceptual analysis drawn from contemporary philosophy of technology, media theory, pedagogy, and AI ethics. Institutional statistical data from international organizations are used descriptively to contextualize the analysis, without serving as primary empirical evidence. Results - The study demonstrates that contemporary digital technologies generate unprecedented levels of illumination in the form of constant visibility and exposure yet lack intrinsic orientational capacity. This form of technological illumination differs structurally from Nūr, which functions as a principle uniting manifestation, intelligibility, and guidance. As a result, digital environments tend to amplify information while weakening meaning, discernment, and interior integration, particularly in the formative experiences of Generation Alpha. Conclusions - The paper concludes that Nūr, employed as a non-confessional metaphysical heuristic, provides a robust ontological criterion for distinguishing between exposure and guidance, correctness and wisdom. This framework offers significant pedagogical and ethical implications for education, writing, and the use of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need to reorient technological practices toward discernment, interiority, and meaningful human understanding.

items.title: Pooja Ramesh Singh V. Jammu and Kashmir bank Ltd. & Another
items.abstract: The case of Pooja Ramesh Singh v. J&K Bank Ltd. represents a significant ruling concerning legal technology in India. The Supreme Court has introduced a policy of zero tolerance towards hallucinated precedents and has stated that any such orders are entirely void, thus protecting the integrity of the judicial record. Since artificial intelligence tools are becoming increasingly common in legal procedures, this judgment makes sure that technology stays a secondary aid to human judgment and therefore upholds the fundamental principles of natural justice, legal accuracy, and judicial accountability.

items.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
items.abstract: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. However, sustainable outcomes depend on reliable data, employee trust, human oversight, privacy protection, algorithmic fairness, and accountable governance. The review proposes an integrated framework linking people, commerce, and marketing capabilities through innovation, efficiency, engagement, and customer value. Future research should empirically test this framework across industries, firm sizes, and national contexts using longitudinal and standardized performance measures. It identifies research priorities concerning human–AI collaboration, digital inclusion, and environmental performance measurement.

items.title: “My Colleagues Are the Ones Who Taught Me Everything”: Navigating Workplace Integration Through Organizational Socialization Among Internationally Recruited Nurses: A Qualitative Descriptive Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: International recruitment is used to address nursing workforce shortages, yet recruitment alone does not ensure successful integration into destination healthcare systems. This study aimed to explore how internationally recruited nurses (IRNs) experience and make sense of workplace integration in Saudi Arabia, with attention to the organizational, relational, and experiential processes that shape integration over time. Methods: A qualitative descriptive study with reflexive thematic analysis was conducted with 19 IRNs in three tertiary hospitals in southern Saudi Arabia. Participants were purposively recruited, and data were generated through semi-structured interviews. Organizational Socialization Theory (OST) was used as a sensitizing theoretical framework rather than a predetermined coding structure. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Four interrelated themes captured participants’ integration experiences: (1) Entering the Workplace with Limited Organizational Preparation; (2) Becoming Integrated Through Workplace Relationships; (3) Learning the Unwritten Workplace Through Experience; and (4) Integration as an Uneven Trajectory Over Time. Formal preparation and orientation were often limited, shifting substantial responsibility for workplace learning to peers, supervisors, and experiential exposure. Supportive relationships facilitated learning and belonging, whereas harsh interactions, perceived inequities, and variable organizational support complicated integration. Conclusions: Workplace integration was experienced as a gradual, relational, and uneven process rather than a discrete orientation event. Healthcare organizations have a central responsibility for supporting integration, while informal peer learning should complement rather than replace structured organizational support.

items.title: A bibliometric analysis of polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity research
items.abstract: Background: Polymyxins remain important therapeutic options for the treatment of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections; however, their clinical application is limited by a narrow therapeutic window and a high risk of nephrotoxicity. Although research on polymyxin-associated nephrotoxicity has expanded rapidly in recent years, the overall evolution of research themes, knowledge structure, and emerging frontiers in this field remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the development trends and research hotspots of polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity using bibliometric analysis. Methods: Relevant publications on polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity published between January 1, 2005, and November 13, 2024, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database. CiteSpace and VOSviewer (Baxter Healthcare Corporation) were used to analyze publication trends, authorship, institutional and country collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, and burst detection. Results: A total of 569 publications were included in this study. The annual publication output demonstrated an overall increasing trend, indicating increasing attention to polymyxin-associated nephrotoxicity research. Li Jian was the most productive author, Monash University was the most productive institution in terms of publication output, and the United States contributed the highest number of publications among all countries. Keyword analysis revealed that research themes have evolved from early characterization of nephrotoxicity and clinical safety assessment toward the identification of acute kidney injury risk factors, elucidation of oxidative stress-related mechanisms, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic optimization, and development of individualized dosing strategies and nephroprotective approaches. Burst analysis further indicated increasing attention toward biomarkers, precision dosing, and novel therapeutic strategies. Conclusion: Bibliometric analysis revealed that research on polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity has progressively evolved from toxicity characterization to mechanistic exploration and precision management. Current challenges include an incomplete understanding of interactions among nephrotoxic pathways, limited dynamic prediction models, and insufficient clinical translation of emerging protective strategies. Future research should focus on integrating multi-omics approaches, artificial intelligence-based risk prediction, therapeutic drug monitoring, and safer polymyxin formulations to optimize the balance between antibacterial efficacy and nephrotoxicity prevention.

items.title: A bioinspired conceptual framework for adaptive university press management
items.abstract: University presses face converging pressures from scholarly quality, peer-review integrity, reviewer scarcity, Open Science, artificial intelligence, international visibility, and economic sustainability. This article proposes Epigenetic Editorial Intelligence, a bioinspired conceptual framework that represents stable institutional rules as Editorial DNA and models operational adaptation through epigenetic regulation, an Artificial Immune System, organizational memory, human–AI collaboration, and multiobjective optimization. Nine operational indicators are formalized and aggregated into a Global Editorial Intelligence Index (GEII). Internal model behavior is examined through paired synthetic ablations that disable one mechanism at a time, using 200 Monte Carlo repetitions, common random-number streams, 95% confidence intervals, alternative weighting schemes and 1000 Dirichlet weight perturbations. Results are interpreted as structural-consistency diagnostics rather than empirical validation. This work provides a reproducible conceptual and mathematical foundation for subsequent implementation and testing with real editorial records.

items.title: A Comparative Study of Client-Level Stabilization Techniques in Federated Learning for Robust Plant Disease Recognition
items.abstract: The successful integration of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in precision agriculture provided farmers with the means to identify potential issues, such as early disease detection or pest infestations, by making crop-related predictions. The new technological developments in this field improve the functioning of traditional agriculture by reducing the dependence on specialized human expertise and facilitating greater access to diagnostic procedures. However, most studies conducted in this area rely on centralized training of AI models, which leads to increased costs and raised privacy-related concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a compelling framework for collaboratively training machine learning (ML) models on distributed datasets without centralizing the data owned by each participant. FL offers significant advantages in the preservation of data privacy, facilitates the collaborative exploitation of geographically distributed data sources, and reduces the risks associated with centralized collection. In this paper, we investigate the current limitations and performance boundaries of existing Federated and privacy-preserving learning in distributed sensing systems for plant disease detection, in scenarios that closely resemble real-world conditions. Our analysis specifically examined how FL aggregation algorithms, such as FedAvg, FedAvgM and FedProx, work in a custom multi-client experimental setup where data is partitioned so that each participant observes only those symptom patterns associated with specific environmental and climatic conditions. We propose further partial aggregation of the local model, an approach where we send only the model backbone to the central server, while the classification head of each participant remains strictly on the client side. The construction of environmentally heterogeneity is combined with a globally representative stabilizer node designed to preserve knowledge across disease classes that may be absent from certain clients.

items.title: A Comprehensive Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis: The Future of Artificial Intelligence in Diagnostic Otology — Opportunities and Barriers to Clinical Implementation
items.abstract: Introduction: Diagnostic otology relies on operator-dependent interpretation of otoscopy, temporal bone computed tomography (CT), audiometry and vestibular testing, and diagnostic accuracy outside specialist settings remains suboptimal. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been proposed as a scalable decision-support solution, but its pooled accuracy, robustness beyond development data, comparative value against clinicians and barriers to clinical implementation have not been synthesised across all diagnostic otology modalities. This review aimed to quantify the diagnostic performance of AI across otoscopic, radiological, audiological and vestibular applications and to map opportunities and barriers to implementation. Methods: The study strictly adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Randomised controlled trials, cohort, case–control and cross-sectional diagnostic studies (prospective or retrospective) evaluating an AI index test against a clinical reference standard were eligible; systematic reviews were excluded from synthesis. Risk of bias was appraised with QUADAS-2 supplemented by QUADAS-AI considerations. Accuracy, sensitivity and specificity were pooled on the logit scale using random-effects models (restricted maximum likelihood with modified Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman confidence intervals) with 95% prediction intervals (PI); risk differences (RD) quantified AI–clinician comparisons. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, influence diagnostics, small-study tests and GRADE certainty assessment were performed. Results: Of 139 unique records, 64 primary studies (2019–2026; otoscopy 37, temporal bone CT 14, audiology 6, vestibular 7) were included. No randomised trial of an AI diagnostic tool in otology was identified. Pooled internal-validation accuracy was 92.5% (95% CI 90.0–94.5) (k = 36; PI 64.7–98.8%; I² = 97.8%, τ² = 0.858): otoscopy 93.2%, temporal bone CT 90.2%, audiometry/tympanometry 97.6% and vestibular testing 84.0% (between-modality P = 0.003). Pooled sensitivity and specificity were 92.6% (95% CI 89.4–94.8) and 89.5% (95% CI 74.3–96.1), respectively (diagnostic odds ratio 105; summary AUROC 0.957). Accuracy fell to 81.2% (95% CI 59.1–92.8) in external, prospective or point-of-care cohorts (P = 0.026 versus internal validation), and studies using surgical, histopathological or objective reference standards reported lower accuracy than those using expert annotation (89.0% vs 93.6%; P = 0.041). Task-specific AI outperformed clinicians on identical cases (RD +18.2 percentage points, 95% CI 7.3 to 29.0), and AI assistance increased clinician accuracy (RD +9.4 points, 95% CI 1.4 to 17.4), whereas general-purpose multimodal large language models underperformed specialists (RD -25.0 points). Of 47 meta-analysed studies, 34 (72.3%) had at least one high risk-of-bias domain; certainty of evidence was low to very low. Discussion: Task-specific AI achieves high diagnostic accuracy across diagnostic otology and consistently exceeds non-specialist performance, supporting its role as a triage and decision-support adjunct, particularly in primary care, tele-otology and resource-limited settings. However, extreme heterogeneity, wide prediction intervals, performance attenuation under domain shift, spectrum and reference-standard bias, scarce prospective evidence and the absence of outcome trials constitute the principal barriers to implementation. Conclusion: AI is a promising but not yet implementation-ready component of diagnostic otology. Multicentre prospective validation with surgical or objective reference standards, standardised image acquisition, transparent reporting (STARD-AI/TRIPOD+AI-aligned) and pragmatic randomised trials measuring patient-important outcomes are required before routine deployment.

items.title: A global machine learning framework for classifying national CO2 emission levels: responsible and explainable artificial intelligence for sustainable climate governance
items.abstract: We investigate whether trade openness, governance, environmental taxation and selected macroeconomic indicators can classify the contemporaneous CO2 emission level of countries observed over 2000 to 2023, using data from the World Development Indicators and the OECD. CO2 emissions per capita are divided into three ordinal levels, low, medium and high, using tertile cut points estimated on the training data only within every validation split. Four classifiers, Random Forest, XGBoost, a support vector machine and a multinomial logistic regression, are tuned and compared alongside two models designed specifically for ordinal outcomes, an ordered logistic regression and an ordinal decomposition of XGBoost, under four validation designs: a country grouped holdout and country grouped 5 fold cross validation, in which no country appears in both the training and test sets; a chronological holdout; a 1 year ahead forecasting task; and a random stratified country year split, retained only as a reference point. Under country grouped cross validation, no classifier achieves a decisively higher accuracy than the others: nested cross validation gives a mean accuracy of 0.644 for XGBoost, 0.648 for Random Forest, 0.671 for the support vector machine, 0.674 for the multinomial logit, 0.676 for the ordered logit and 0.637 for the ordinal XGBoost model, with overlapping confidence intervals throughout. This is markedly lower than the 0.91 accuracy obtained under a random country year split with the same tuned pipeline, a gap of 12.5 percentage points for XGBoost, confirming that a substantial part of the high accuracy obtainable under random splitting reflects the model recognizing previously seen country profiles rather than generalizing to unseen countries. Accuracy falls less sharply under the chronological holdout and the 1 year ahead forecasting task, in the region of 0.65 to 0.74, indicating that the classifiers generalize better across time within a country than across countries. Permutation importance, SHAP and LIME consistently identify government effectiveness, urban population growth and environmental tax revenue as the features most strongly associated with model predictions, with a moderate contribution from trade openness and the smallest from GDP growth, a ranking that is stable across importance methods, learning algorithms and cross validation folds. These variables are predictors of the model's output, not estimated causal determinants of emissions, and the results are best read as evidence for climate risk monitoring and further policy evaluation rather than as a causal policy assessment.

items.title: A hybrid reinforcement learning and Harris Hawks Optimization framework for multi-objective resource management in IIoT
items.abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is revolutionizing industrial processes by interconnecting sensors, machines, and computing resources to enable intelligent automation, real-time monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Despite its potential, efficient allocation and management of resources in IIoT networks remain a significant challenge due to the dynamic, heterogeneous, and large-scale nature of industrial environments. Traditional static or heuristic resource allocation methods often fail to satisfy conflicting objectives such as minimizing latency, maximizing throughput, ensuring energy efficiency, and maintaining system reliability. To address these challenges, this paper presents the design and development of an AI-based multi-objective resource management system for IIoT systems. The system integrates reinforcement learning (RL) for adaptive, real-time decision-making with Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) for multi-objective optimization, balancing competing performance metrics across sensing, communication, computing, and control layers. The RL agent predicts system states and dynamically adjusts resource allocation, while HHO fine-tunes the solutions to achieve optimal performance under multiple constraints. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms conventional static and heuristic approaches, achieving higher efficiency, faster adaptability, and improved scalability. By intelligently managing resources and optimizing system behavior, this system enhances overall operational reliability and Quality-of-Service in IIoT networks. The results indicate that combining AI-driven decision-making with advanced nature-inspired optimization provides a robust and efficient solution for next-generation industrial applications, paving the way for more intelligent, resilient, and resource-efficient IIoT systems.

items.title: A Lifelong Neuro-Symbolic Explainable AI Twin for Zero-Touch 6G IoE Management Under Non-Stationary Network Dynamics
items.abstract: Future sixth-generation (6G) Internet of Everything (IoE) networks require zero-touch management systems capable of autonomously allocating communication and computational resources, satisfying service-level constraints, and providing transparent explanations for their decisions. Existing neuro-symbolic explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) twins improve interpretability by coupling neural prediction with symbolic reasoning; however, most rely on statically engineered causal graphs, fixed rule sets, and immutable knowledge bases. Such closed-world assumptions are unsuitable for non-stationary 6G environments in which radio conditions, mobility patterns, interference relationships, and service requirements continuously evolve. To address this limitation, this paper proposes LL-NS-XAI, a Lifelong Learning Neuro-Symbolic XAI Digital Twin for zero-touch 6G IoE management. The framework integrates three tightly coupled planes: an online implicit learner at the physical edge for time-varying service association and uplink/downlink resource allocation; a dynamic explicit learner in the virtual core for directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based Bayesian reasoning, most-probable-explanation inference, and explainable trust scoring; and a meta-cognitive layer that monitors reasoning residuals, detects parameter drift, structural drift, and ontological emergence, and autonomously revises the causal graph, probabilistic rule sets, conditional probability tables, and knowledge base. Unlike static neuro-symbolic twins, LL-NS-XAI treats realized post-decision outcomes, including achieved channel quality indicator (CQI), measured end-to-end delay, and throughput, as interventional evidence for online causal-model adaptation. Experimental evaluation using a non-stationary 5G-derived dataset with injected parameter drift, structural drift, and emergent IoE service classes demonstrates that LL-NS-XAI maintains higher long-term trustworthiness, lower reasoning residuals, and bounded performance degradation compared with static XAI twins, non-stationary bandits, and pure continual-learning baselines. The framework additionally accommodates a previously unseen IoE service class through autonomous causal-graph expansion, recovering near-oracle performance without offline retraining. These results demonstrate that lifelong causal adaptation can improve the robustness, explainability, and autonomy of AI-enabled zero-touch management in evolving 6G IoE networks.

items.title: A multi-stage validation framework for trustworthy large-scale clinical information extraction using large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) show promise for extracting clinically meaningful information from unstructured health records, yet real-world deployment is constrained by limited scalable, trustworthy validation approaches. Conventional evaluation relies on annotation-intensive reference standards and incomplete structured data, limiting population-scale use. We propose a multi-stage validation framework for LLM-based clinical information extraction that enables rigorous assessment under weak supervision by integrating complementary validation strategies. The framework combines prompt calibration, rule-based filtering, semantic grounding, judge-LLM evaluation, expert review, and predictive validity analysis to quantify uncertainty without exhaustive manual annotation. We applied this framework to extract substance use disorder (SUD) diagnoses across 11 substance categories from 919,783 clinical notes. Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported or structurally implausible. For high-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert. Using judge evaluations as references, the primary LLM achieved an F1 score of 0.80. LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines. By unifying complementary validation strategies, this work presents a generalizable human-in-the-loop framework for establishing the trustworthiness of LLM-based clinical information extraction at scale while minimizing the need for exhaustive manual annotation.

items.title: A neutrophil-specific GSR integrates pattern recognition receptor in pathogenesis of neonatal late-onset sepsis: evidence from artificial intelligence-driven multi-omics and clinical validation
items.abstract: Abstract Background Neonatal late-onset sepsis (NS) is a life-threatening condition driven by a dysregulated host response to infection, where neutrophil dysfunction plays a pivotal role. Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), as the frontline sensors of the innate immune system, are increasingly recognized as key regulators of immune cell function, yet their specific connection to neutrophil biology in NS remains largely undefined. Objective This study aimed to decode a novel PRR-neutrophil (PRRN)-associated molecular signature in NS. Methods Bulk transcriptomic data from NS peripheral samples (GSE138712) were analyzed using Limma, WGCNA, and CIBERSORT to identify shared PRRN-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Hub genes were narrowed down via PPI network analysis. A diagnostic model was constructed using 132 machine learning algorithms on the training set (GSE69686, NS peripheral blood bulk profile) and validated on an independent set (GSE25504, NS peripheral blood bulk profile) based on PRRN-associated hub genes. SHAP analysis identified the central hub gene in training set. Single-cell RNA sequencing data of sepsis patient peripheral blood(GSE167363) were used to validate its cell-specific distribution, functional trajectory, and regulatory network at spatial and temporal manners via cutting-edge analytical framework. AI-based drug screening (DrugReflector) and molecular docking computationally nominated a candidate therapeutic compound for NS targeting PRRN-associated central hub genes. Finally, NS patient clinical samples were collected for the validation of expression patterns of hub genes. Results We identified PRRN-associated diagnostic and candidate therapeutic models for NS patients and nominated GSR as the PRRN-associated and up-regulated hub gene in NS pathogenesis. Single-cell analysis confirmed that GSR is predominantly expressed in neutrophils within the NS samples and is enriched in pathways related to innate immune response. Conclusion This study systematically defines novel PRRN molecular co-expression patterns in NS, establishing GSR as a neutrophil-centric hub gene. These findings offer a potential diagnostic framework and an exploratory therapeutic target for NS patients, and the candidate compound requires further experimental validation.

items.title: A qualitative study on professional caregiver burden among healthcare professionals in Parkinson’s disease in Chennai, India
items.abstract: Healthcare professionals experience substantial burden when providing long-term care for patients with Parkinson’s disease. Despite their central role in care delivery, the experiences of healthcare professionals remain under-examined in Indian healthcare contexts. This qualitative study explored professional caregiver burden among healthcare professionals involved in Parkinson’s disease care in South India. Twelve healthcare professionals (Neurologists, Nurses, Physician Assistants, Physiotherapists, and Psychologists) were recruited from two tertiary hospitals in Chennai between April and May 2025. A semi-structured interview schedule was utilised to gather data. Data were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis. The study identified 5 major themes (1) Emotional Burden of Continuous Care in PD, (2) Clinical and Cognitive Complexity, (3) Critical Care and Physical Demands, (4) Family Dynamics and Relative Challenges, and (5) Administrative and Systemic Barriers, encompassing 18 sub-themes. The findings indicate that professional caregiver burden in PD care arises from the interaction of cultural expectations, structural constraints, and the progressive nature of the disease. Remarkably, accumulated clinical experience did not diminish cognitive burden; instead, greater experience escalated exposure to therapeutic uncertainty and prognostic complexity. Findings associated with physical rehabilitation are presented as an illustrative case, due to the single-participant illustration of the physiotherapy discipline. The professional caregiver burden among healthcare professionals in PD care operates across multiple professional and systemic dimensions. It also represents a patient-safety concern with implications for occupational health policy and institutional mental-health support in tertiary care settings. These burden dimensions elucidate how professional caregiver burden, emerging from progressive neurological disease care, is shaped by structural constraints and cultural care contexts.

items.title: A qualitative typology of teachers’ orientations toward artificial intelligence integration in Lebanese schools
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping educational practices, requiring teachers to develop new competencies while navigating complex ethical considerations. This qualitative study explores the perceptions, practices, and orientations of 28 Lebanese schoolteachers regarding the integration of AI in school settings. Findings indicate that while a majority of participants reported familiarity with AI, only a limited proportion integrated AI into their instructional practices. Reported barriers included insufficient training, lack of institutional support, and concerns related to data privacy and ethical use. The analysis led to the identification of three qualitative orientations toward AI integration—reluctant users, early adopters, and critical skeptics—reflecting differentiated levels of readiness and engagement. The findings highlight the need for context-sensitive, pedagogically grounded, and ethically informed professional development to support sustainable AI integration in education.

items.title: A recall-optimized LSTM–XGBoost ensemble model for river flood forecasting using multivariate time-series data—case study in Sri Lanka
items.abstract: Riverine (fluvial) flooding remains a significant climate-related disaster in many countries. Extreme rainfall events caused by climate change cause significant damage and disruption to communities living near riverbanks or neighboring land areas, particularly when risk-sensitive development is ignored. This necessitates an effective mechanism to predict river flooding events and provide timely early warnings to the most vulnerable populations in high-risk flood-prone areas. The dynamics of flood risks require a localized, automated, and scalable solution that can be centrally monitored. This study presents a river flood forecasting system integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT). This system was deployed in one of the flood-prone river basins in Sri Lanka to assess the operational feasibility of real-time hydrological monitoring and flood-risk classification. The proposed system employed two machine learning models, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), for flood-risk prediction and IoT sensors (rainfall and ultrasonic sensors) for real-time hydrological data collection. The machine learning models were developed using rainfall, discharge rate, and river water level data to predict flood-risk states. A rule-based ensemble strategy was implemented by combining the outputs of LSTM and XGBoost to prioritize positive-class detection and reduce missed positive-labeled observations. Model performance was evaluated primarily using recall for the positive flood cases, while the overall accuracy was reported as the complementary metric alongside positive-class recall, providing an overall assessment of classification performance. Among the evaluated input window configurations using the same chronological holdout, the rule-based ensemble model with a 1-day input window showed the most favorable observed balance of performance metrics, achieving 100% positive-class recall, with 98.73% accuracy, 50.00% positive-class precision, and 66.67% positive-class F1-score. The 100.00% recall was based on correctly classifying all four positive-labeled observations in the held-out test set (4/4; 95% exact binomial CI: 39.8%−100.0%) and these observations occurred consecutively from November 25 to 28, 2024, and represent one continuous positive-labeled flood episode. The proposed safety-oriented AI-IoT framework demonstrates the operational feasibility of integrating real-time sensing with AI-based flood forecasting; however, longer-term field deployment, including actual flood events, is required to evaluate flood-event prediction performance under real-world flood conditions.

items.title: A Review of AI-Based Women Safety and Emergency Response Systems
items.abstract: Women's safety applications have increasingly adopted mobile sensing, Global Positioning System (GPS), cloud services, and artificial intelligence to support emergency communication and risk awareness. However, existing systems differ considerably in their methods of detecting emergencies and responding to them. Some applications primarily provide manual SOS functions and location sharing, while others introduce voice activation, contextual risk assessment, offline communication, predictive analysis, or evidence collection. This paper reviews recent technology-based women safety and emergency response systems, with particular attention to their emergency triggers, use of artificial intelligence, location services, evidence collection, communication mechanisms, and limitations. The reviewed literature covers mobile applications, predictive safety systems, contextual monitoring, and cloud-supported emergency platforms. The analysis shows that current solutions have improved the speed and accessibility of emergency assistance, but several systems remain focused on individual functions rather than integrated risk detection and response. Important gaps remain in continuous behaviour analysis, anomaly detection, automatic triggering, reliable operation under limited connectivity, evidence management, and reduction of false alarms. Based on these observations, the paper discusses a proposed research direction for an integrated AI-based women safety platform designed to combine predictive risk assessment, multiple emergency triggers, location tracking, evidence collection, and automated emergency response.

items.title: A review of recent advances in privacy-preserving federated learning for healthcare applications
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare, driven by the increasing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging systems, genomic data, and wearable devices, has created significant challenges related to patient privacy, data security, and regulatory compliance. Traditional centralised machine learning (ML) approaches often require large-scale data sharing, which increases the risk of sensitive medical information exposure. Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising distributed learning paradigm that enables collaborative model training across multiple institutions without transferring raw patient data. Recent advances in privacy-preserving FL have further strengthened its applicability in healthcare through the integration of techniques such as differential privacy (DP), homomorphic encryption (HE), secure aggregation, blockchain-assisted frameworks, and secure multi-party computation. This study critically reviews recent developments in privacy-preserving FL for healthcare applications published between 2024 and early 2026, with particular emphasis on medical imaging, EHRs analytics, genomics, and wearable health monitoring systems. In addition, major technical and security challenges, including non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions, communication overhead, scalability issues, gradient leakage, model poisoning, and membership inference attacks, are comprehensively analysed. Regulatory, ethical, and interoperability concerns associated with cross-institutional collaboration are also discussed. Finally, current research gaps, emerging trends, and future directions for developing secure, scalable, and trustworthy federated healthcare systems are identified.

items.title: A Review of Virtual Power Plant Technology and Practice Development in China: Progress, Challenges, and Outlook
items.abstract: As an important vehicle for resource integration in the construction of new power systems, the virtual power plant (VPP) has moved from the demonstration and pilot stage into a critical transition period of standardized construction and market-oriented operation. This paper systematically reviews the technological development trajectory and the practical progress of VPPs in China. At the technical level, key advances are reviewed across three core domains: resource perception and adjustable potential assessment; optimal dispatch and control strategies (covering centralized, distributed, and reinforcement learning-based methods); and cloud–edge–terminal platform architecture and information security. At the practical level, the paper traces the policy evolution from the early demand response pilots to the 2025 Guiding Opinions on Accelerating the Development of Virtual Power Plants, surveys grid-led and third-party-aggregator demonstration projects, and analyzes business models and pathways for participation in electricity markets. On this basis, the key challenges facing Chinese VPPs in technical standardization, market access, regulatory frameworks, and data security are analyzed, and international experience from Europe (Next Kraftwerke, Flexitricity), North America (FERC Order 2222), and Australia (Tesla VPP) is summarized. Finally, future development pathways are discussed from four directions: technological trends (digital twins and the integration of large language models), the improvement of market mechanisms, the construction of the policy and standards system, and the cultivation of a multi-stakeholder industrial ecosystem.

items.title: A Review on Alumni–Student Engagement Systems and AI Recommenders in Higher Education
items.abstract: Alumni–student engagement has evolved from static communication into a dynamic, data-driven ecosystem. Traditionalalumni management platforms primarily focus on event coordination and record maintenance, but lack personalization, intelligence, and adaptive interaction. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) enable the automation of mentor– mentee matching based on skills, interests, and professional attributes, thereby enhancing the relevance and quality of alumni–student interactions. This paper reviews existing alumni engagement systems, identifies key technological limitations, and emphasizes the growing need for AI-based recommendation mechanisms within academic ecosystems. While visualization dashboards continue to support transparency and performance tracking, AI-driven recommendations emerge as the core enabler of personalized engagement. The paper integrates insights from contemporary literature and proposes a conceptual direction for building intelligent, scalable, and institution-centric engagement platforms.

items.title: A Review on Digital Twin with AI Based Predictive Maintenance System
items.abstract: Predictive maintenance reduces unexpected machine failures and downtime by continuously observing equipment condition and identifying abnormal behaviour before severe failure occurs. This review paper examines recent research on Digital Twin (DT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, multi-sensor condition monitoring, and predictive maintenance of industrial machines, with emphasis on induction motors. Based on the reviewed literature, a low-cost integrated architecture is proposed using temperature, vibration, current, and RPM sensing, an ESP32 controller, AI-based fault prediction, Digital Twin updating, and IoT-based monitoring. Random Forest is considered as the main classification model because related literature demonstrates strong performance for motor-fault classification. Sample formulas for RMS vibration, mean, variance, RPM, and percentage change are presented. The proposed workflow connects physical sensing, data processing, AI prediction, virtual representation, alert generation, and predictive-maintenance decision support. Illustrative graphs are included only as sample results and must be replaced by measured experimental data before final validation.

items.title: A Rewrite That Keeps the Label Has Already Read It: Why an LLM Paraphrase Can Raise a Sentiment Classifier's Accuracy Without the Classifier Getting Better, Four Accounts of the Gain, and the Re-Annotation and Neutral-Rate Controls That Would Separate Them
items.abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. A 2026 study reports that sentiment classifiers score higher on reviews rewritten by small language models than on the human originals, by up to 5.8 accuracy points, and reads the gain as stylistic alignment: the rewrite strips idiosyncrasy and hands the classifier text closer to what it was trained on. It concludes that benchmarks cleaned or paraphrased by language models will overstate classifier performance. Two older literatures point the other way. Paraphrase and style-transfer attacks drive the same classifiers down, and a 2025 study of fifty thousand rephrased tweets finds that rewriting pulls sentiment toward neutral, a pull its robustness checks found again when the prompt asked for the sentiment to be kept. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that neither direction measures the classifier alone, because every one of these designs scores the rewritten text against the label of the text it replaced. The paper separates four accounts of a rewrite-induced gain: alignment of style with the classifier's training data; a fall in the rate of neutral predictions, which the anchor's scoring counts as errors; the paraphraser acting as an annotator that decides the polarity and then writes it plainly; and the removal of hard, mixed and ironic items. It shows from the anchor's released code that its prompt demands one of two polarities and that a neutral prediction is always scored wrong, that its own count of label flips is mislabelled: the printed 291 is the net gain, not the number of improvements, and that a test-time rewriting study found rewritten inputs still sitting with the out-of-distribution data in embedding space. The paper consolidates the measured values in two tables and a figure, states a licensing procedure as an algorithm, counts from the anchor's released predictions that a fall in neutral predictions carries about half of the largest gain, and names the re-annotation, paraphraser-baseline and prompt-ablation controls that would settle which account holds for the rest.

items.title: A Student-Centered Model for Ethically Evaluating AI Integration in Learning Support Services and Beyond
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes higher education, learning support centers are uniquely positioned to intentionally assess whether if and how to best integrate AI tools into academic services. This session presents a 6-week project framework that was designed to: • Review the literature on critical AI literacy and training • Benchmark current best practices in AI policy, use, and integration alongside human-centered academic services • Examine student AI knowledge and use (needs assessment) • Identify and evaluate relevant AI tools or platforms The framework was developed within the Academic Success Center (ASC) at Nevada State University where Center peer educators (student employees) served as project leads and evaluators. This model offers a practical, research-informed pathway for institutions seeking to lead responsibly in AI-integrated learning support or other student services. Session activities include a walkthrough and discussion of the model structure, tools, challenges, and recommendations. Attendees will leave with: (1) a sample 6-week project roadmap, (2) a student-centered model for AI evaluation and pilot design, (3) learning frameworks grounded in critical AI literacy, (4) adaptable resources for assessment and decision-making, and (5) strategies for positioning students as co-creators in institutional/unit change

items.title: A study of the impact of AI-employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior
items.abstract: Introduction With the deep integration of digitalization and generative artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence has transformed from a mere technical tool into a core collaborative partner within modern workplaces and human‑resource management. As an interdependent human‑AI working mode characterized by complementary task division, joint task accomplishment, complementary decision‑making, and continuous iterative interaction between employees and AI agents, AI‑employee collaboration is conceptually distinct from simple AI adoption, instrumental AI use, and AI‑assisted technical systems. Drawing on social cognitive theory, the present study aims to investigate how AI‑employee collaboration predicts employee innovation behavior, alongside the mediating role of self‑efficacy and the moderated‑mediation boundary condition of servant leadership. Methods Three‑wave time‑lagged questionnaire data were collected from 259 employees working in internet‑service, finance, and catering industries across Beijing and Jinan. Hierarchical regression and bootstrap approaches were adopted to test the proposed moderated‑mediation model. Results The results show that AI‑employee collaboration exerts a significant positive predictive effect on employee innovation behavior. Self‑efficacy partially mediates the relationship between AI‑employee collaboration and employee innovation behavior. Moreover, servant leadership positively moderates the link between AI‑employee collaboration and self‑efficacy and further strengthens the indirect predictive effect of AI‑employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior through self‑efficacy. Discussion This research enriches existing literature by providing incremental empirical evidence for the internal cognitive mechanism and contextual boundary of AI‑driven employee innovation. Theoretically, it unpacks the cognitive “black box” connecting AI‑employee collaboration and employee innovation and identifies servant leadership as a key situational contingency factor. Practically, these findings deliver concrete, actionable managerial insights for digitally transforming organizations to leverage AI tools and unlock employees’ innovative potential.

items.abstract: The study “A Study on the Influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Literacy on Career Readiness Among Young Adults in Chennai” aims to establish a connection between the level of awareness about AI and career readiness. The influence of artificial intelligence is increasing in all fields of activity, especially in the educational and professional spheres. Therefore, understanding the characteristics of this technology is becoming a vital skill for achieving employability in the future. The study uses a descriptive research design, with a primary data collection method. The data was gathered by distributing questionnaires among one hundred respondents who were selected using a convenience sampling technique. The data analysis involved the percentage analysis of the results, the weighted average of the responses, multiple linear regression, and Pearson’s correlation. items.title: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence ( AI )‐Based Task Scheduling Techniques for Cloud‐Fog Computing Environments
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid proliferation of latency‐sensitive and data‐intensive applications has accelerated the adoption of cloud–fog computing architectures to support real‐time processing and distributed resource management. However, efficient task scheduling in cloud–fog environments remains a challenging problem because of resource heterogeneity, dynamic workloads, network variability, and stringent quality of service (QoS) requirements. Artificial intelligence (AI)‐based techniques, including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and hybrid AI approaches, have emerged as promising solutions for addressing these challenges. This paper presents a systematic review of AI‐based task scheduling techniques in cloud–fog computing environments published between 2021 and 2025. Following a PRISMA‐inspired methodology, 74 high‐quality studies were selected and analyzed. The reviewed works are classified into ML, DL, DRL, and hybrid AI‐based scheduling categories and evaluated with respect to scheduling objectives, QoS parameters, datasets, evaluation tools, and implementation environments. The analysis reveals that AI‐driven scheduling approaches significantly improve key performance metrics, including task scheduling performance (14%–90%), latency reduction (15%–65%), energy optimization (15%–41%), load balancing (20%–45%), execution time reduction (15%–45%), and cost optimization (10%–32%). This review further highlights the increasing adoption of DL, DRL, and hybrid AI techniques for managing complex and dynamic cloud–fog infrastructures. Additionally, this study identifies critical research challenges, including scalability, resource heterogeneity, lack of standardized benchmark datasets, limited real‐world deployments, and insufficient consideration of network‐layer dynamics. Finally, emerging research directions and future opportunities for developing scalable, adaptive, and intelligent scheduling frameworks in cloud–fog computing environments are discussed. items.title: A Web Engineering Approach to AI-Enabled Japanese Tutoring via Instructional Design Pattern Mining
items.abstract: Despite the proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled web applications for Japanese language learning, existing platforms suffer from three critical challenges: insufficient integration of AI capabilities with pedagogical design, limited scenario adaptability across proficiency levels, and suboptimal lightweight deployment on the browser side. To address these gaps and explore instructional design patterns tailored to diverse Japanese learning needs, this study focuses on web application technology implementation and interaction design as the core analytical dimensions. Three typical AI-enabled Japanese tutoring web applications were selected as research objects, and 192 Japanese learners participated in the empirical research. Quantitative data were obtained through technical disassembly, questionnaire surveys, and web-based behavior tracking; learning effects were verified by comparative experiments, and the weight of instructional design elements was determined via the analytic hierarchy process, finally extracting core instructional design modes suitable for the mainstream Japanese learning stages from beginner to upper-intermediate (Japanese-Language Proficiency Test [JLPT] N5–N2), with preliminary applicability discussion for the advanced stage (N1 and above). The results show that web-based lightweight AI technology deployment and real-time AI interactive feedback design are the core elements, with a combined weight of over 40%. There is a significant positive correlation between web-based AI technology implementation and user satisfaction, with the highest implementation effect and user acceptance in listening, speaking, and grammar modules. Compared with traditional Japanese web learning platforms, AI-enabled instructional design can improve learners’ listening and speaking abilities by 58.0%(M=58.0,SD=4.2,95% CI [56.4, 59.6], Cohen’s d=1.82, large effect), grammar analysis abilities by 46.5% (M=46.5,SD=5.1,95%CI [44.8, 48.2], Cohen’s d=1.45, large effect), and enhance learning sustainability by 85.7% (M=85.7,SD=6.3,95%CI[83.5,87.9], Cohen’s d=2.01, large effect), based on N5–N2 learner data with robust statistical power. Three core instructional design modes were identified, adapted to zero-based-N4 fragmented learning, N3–N2 systematic learning, and N1+ immersive learning, respectively. This study clarifies the core elements and optimization direction of such applications, providing standardized and practical theoretical references and paths for their design, development, and teaching practice.

items.title: Adaptive interaction in intelligent augmented reality: design decision considerations and framework
items.abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Augmented Reality (AR) systems has evolved AR from a passive visualization tool into an intelligent medium for dynamic task execution. For this new role, Intelligent Augmented Reality (IAR) systems must adapt user interfaces (UIs) in real-time to users’ cognitive and physical states, task requirements, and environmental constraints, which raises foundational questions: what design decisions contribute to useful adaptive interaction? To address this question, this paper presents a systematic review of IAR systems through the lens of interaction design at the intersection of AR technologies , AI integration , and User Experience (UX) considerations . After screening 798 peer-reviewed works, 241 full-text records were assessed for eligibility. We reviewed 24 IAR published works based on their interaction features, including proactivity versus reactivity and communication styles and modalities, as well as their types of adaptation and control dynamics. Analyzing these features led to the development of a taxonomy for Levels of Automation and a top-down design framework for adaptive UIs in IAR Systems. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of assistive interaction and semi-autonomous IAR systems that achieve a balanced integration of adaptive assistance with prioritizing user agency while also revealing a noticeable gap in implicit understanding within current IAR implementations.

items.title: Addressing symbolic obstacles in undergraduate calculus through artificial intelligence scaffolding
items.abstract: Symbolic obstacles in calculus prevent students from moving away from intuition and towards formal thinking, but are rarely studied in the context of artificial intelligence (AI) interaction logs. We investigated symbolic obstacles and AI-supported representational transitions among 12 Indonesian undergraduate mathematics education students in a non-intrusive intrinsic case study. Semi-structured interviews, eight classroom observations, diagnostic tests, academic artifacts, and AI logs were analyzed through inductive-deductive thematic analysis, based on Tall’s Three Worlds of Mathematics. Four obstacles are highlighted: graph-to-symbol translation, integral and sigma notation, limit notation, and symbolic algebraic manipulation. Participant-level comparisons showed 27.4%–53.8% fewer coded symbolic errors in post-activity assessments than at baseline. AI scaffolding through dynamic visualization, adaptive feedback, step-by-step guidance, and solution validation was associated with representational cycling, metacognitive reflection, reported self-efficacy gains, and lower mathematics anxiety. The study integrates AI-log evidence with the Three Worlds framework to explain how scaffolding can support students in addressing symbolic obstacles.

items.title: ADMP-GCN: Interpretable Adaptive Message Passing Graph Learning for Patient-specific EEG Seizure Prediction with Human-in-the-Loop Validation
items.abstract: Automated seizure prediction based on multichannel Electroencephalography (EEG) using Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a challenging task that mandates accurate and interpretable results for improved clinical decisionmaking.However, brain connectivity modelling on the evolving patient-specific and seizure-dynamic EEG signals makes the problem highly complex.Recently, Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based approaches have shown promising results for improved seizure prediction by modelling brain functional connectivity and inter-channel interactions.However, they employ redundant channel representations and a fixed propagation mechanism, which potentially limit their practicality.To address these potential limitations, this paper introduces a unified framework that employs an explanation-constrained topology-aware graph learning model.In this context, a novel Adaptive Depth Message Passing Graph Convolutional Network (ADMP-GCN) is introduced that models topology-conditioned message propagation to enable heterogeneous receptive fields within EEG connectivity graphs while considering channel reduction for improved efficiency and robustness.Following model training, multilevel post hoc explainability is performed using SHAP, Integrated Gradients (IG), and GNNExplainer to interpret feature, layer, and graph-level contributions to seizure prediction.Finally, a human-aligned composite supervision is introduced that balances prediction accuracy and explanation quality.The proposed model is validated using the CHB-MIT dataset, and it is found that the proposed model results in improved accuracy of 95.10% and sensitivity of 96.33% compared to existing graph-based seizure prediction models.In conclusion, the results reveal a viable and clinically relevant seizure prediction that balances performance and applicability.

items.abstract: Abstract The research study seeks to investigate the adoption of Artificial Intelligence enabled digital banking on micro, small and medium enterprises led by women in Mumbai suburbs. Though AI is transforming the banking and financial services by improving easy access to banking services, efficiency and security, still informal MSME’S faces lack of reach of such services due to various infant stages especially among women entrepreneurs. The proposed study aims to identify the vast potential in the MSME sector undertaken by women particularly in Mumbai suburbs. The area under study have limited access to digital banking and financial services. Though MSMEs form the backbone of developing and developed nations, yet there is a constant barrier in adopting digital banking services. This paper investigates the transformative role of AI enabling for easy digital banking accessibility in their day-to-day financial transactions especially cross-sectional groups. The study evaluates the readiness of technology adoption, organizational compatibility and perceived trust with special reference TAM (Technology Acceptance Model) integration in women-led MSMEs. The study explores the level of awareness about AI it is ways to AI adoption, and enabling factors in it and its outcome on MSMEs performance. Adoption correlates positively with women entrepreneurs, digital literacy, access to finance and supportive local networks. The research study more specific to the Mumbai suburban area. Most of the MSMEs run by women entrepreneurship are informal in doing business. They lack proper documentation related to their business and financial transactions. Sometime this may lead to bias. Due to the current significant development of Artificial Intelligence in the financial sector the research study related to adoption may tend to shift to other newer features. The study concludes by developing a comprehensive framework showing the drivers influencing the adoption of AI in digital banking among the women-led entrepreneurs. Further in the research it provides insights to the policy makers to consider the women-led entrepreneurs requirements in their financial polices Keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital banking, MSME, TAM (Technology Acceptance Model) integration.

items.title: Adrian Monk – The Obsessive Eye of Justice
items.abstract: Chapter 5 examines Adrian Monk’s extraordinary observational abilities through the lens of cognitive science, neurodivergence, and ethical investigation. Monk’s compulsive attention to detail, pattern recognition, and environmental scanning parallels advanced forensic analysis and situational awareness training. The chapter explores how Monk’s neurodivergent traits, hyperfocus, sensory sensitivity, and intolerance for disorder enhance his investigative accuracy but also present personal and ethical challenges. Students learn how Monk’s methods resemble cognitive interviewing, micro-pattern detection, and anomaly recognition used in intelligence analysis. Chapter 5 also addresses the portrayal of mental health in crime fiction, emphasizing the importance of respectful representation and the real-world value of diverse cognitive strengths in investigative work. Ultimately, Monk illustrates how unconventional thinking can reveal hidden truths and how ethical frameworks must guide the use of extraordinary perceptual abilities.

items.title: Advanced AI/ML Analysis of AQI to Study the Crowd Density Effect
items.abstract: Public environments can experience rapid changes in person density, particularly during festivals, weekends, and special occasions. These changes may influence carbon dioxide concentration, particulate matter, temperature, humidity, and the resulting air-quality condition. This paper presents an integrated framework that combines camera-based person counting with environmental sensing and artificial intelligence and machine learning analysis. A vision module estimates the number of people and crowd density from video frames, while environmental observations are collected with synchronized timestamps. The combined dataset is preprocessed, aligned, and analyzed to identify relationships between crowd density and air-quality indicators. The framework also supports dashboard-based visualization and alert generation for practical monitoring. The proposed approach is intended to provide a common analytical view of occupancy and environmental conditions in public premises. Since experimental measurements are not included in the supplied project material, numerical performance results are not claimed in this paper; the evaluation structure is defined for completion after data collection.

items.title: ADVANCES IN AI-BASED PERSONALIZED HEALTHCARE
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly changing the way healthcare is delivered by supporting a more personalized and patient-centered approach to medicine. Personalized medicine combines information such as genetics, genomics, medical history, lifestyle, laboratory results, medical images, and continuous health data to help healthcare professionals make better decisions for individual patients. Its applications include disease risk prediction, AI-assisted medical imaging, genomic data interpretation, biomarker identification, personalized drug selection, pharmacogenomics, adaptive drug dosing, treatment response prediction, and remote patient monitoring through wearable and mobile health technologies. However, successful implementation requires careful data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, model development, validation, and continuous monitoring. Despite its benefits, AI-driven personalized medicine faces important challenges, including data privacy and security, poor data quality, limited diversity in datasets, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, high implementation costs, and regulatory and ethical concerns. Future developments such as digital twins, generative AI, precision oncology, multi-omics integration, federated learning, and real-time adaptive treatment systems may further strengthen personalized healthcare. Overall, AI should complement rather than replace healthcare professionals, providing evidence-based support while keeping patient safety, fairness, privacy, and clinical judgment at the center of care.

items.title: Agencia docente e inteligencia artificial generativa en educación: análisis bibliométrico y mapeo científico (2022–2026)
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has introduced new forms of assistance, automation, and co-production in teaching, intensifying debates about teacher agency, pedagogical judgment, and professional autonomy. This study aimed to characterize the evolution, thematic structure, and research fronts connecting teacher agency with generative artificial intelligence between 2022 and 10 September 2026. An exploratory bibliometric analysis was conducted on a verified corpus of 30 DOI-bearing publications retrieved through structured searches of open scholarly metadata and cross-checked against publisher records. Temporal productivity, source concentration, conceptual recurrence, and thematic relationships were examined. Output was absent in 2022, incipient in 2023-2024, and accelerated in 2025-2026, which accounted for 80.0% of the corpus. Mapping identified four clusters: agency and professional judgment, teacher education, professional knowledge for AI integration, and assessment-governance. items.title: Agentic Delegation Charter: A Preliminary Terminological and Governance Proposal
items.abstract: Abstract This research note introduces the proposed designation Agentic Delegation Charter (ADC), alongside its French equivalent, Charte de délégation agentique, within the research programme of Blooming Semantics Institute (BSI). Drawing on established project management principles, the proposal outlines a governance framework for successive delegations involving artificial intelligence agents. Three interdependent principles are identified: recursive project governance, whereby each successive delegation is treated as a subordinate project subject to the overarching charter; terminological invariance and semantic continuity, supported by an authoritative project-specific lexicon; and distributed authority, governed through explicit conditions of authorization, competence, accountability, and control. The note also identifies challenges concerning semantic interpretation, the evolution of delegated authority, human oversight, and the temporal constraints of decision-making. Its purpose is to document a preliminary terminological and conceptual proposal dated 16 October 2026, without claiming exclusive authorship of the expression or establishing scientific originality prior to a comprehensive review of the literature.

items.title: AgenticInspect: Risk-Aware Segmentation Refinement with Hybrid Auditing for Electronic Interconnection Inspection in Smart Manufacturing
items.abstract: Industrial visual inspection requires not only accurate segmentation but also reliable and traceable decision making, since incorrect automatic refinements may lead to downstream manufacturing failures. Although segmentation foundation models achieve strong segmentation accuracy, they provide limited support for assessing whether refinement actions should be accepted, rejected, or escalated before deployment. To address this challenge, we propose AgenticInspect, a hybrid-audited agentic inspection framework that reformulates segmentation refinement as an action-level, risk-aware decision process. AgenticInspect treats an edge-deployable segmentation model as a replaceable skill. Based on the output of the segmentation skill, AgenticInspect introduces three task-specific decision modules, including uncertainty- and geometry-guided candidate generation, train-learned gating for high-risk refinement actions, and hybrid audit for risk-controlled mask selection. The hybrid audit layer integrates deterministic safety rules, train-learned safety gates, and selective large language model (LLM) review. The proposed framework provides action-level risk control and auditable decision making, with a traceable rationale for accepting, rejecting, or escalating candidate refinements. AgenticInspect was evaluated on a labeled connector-inspection dataset. The proposed refinement pipeline improved IoU from 0.9189303 to 0.9190180. The full hybrid policy reduced degraded refinements from 14 to 12 while maintaining nearly all performance gains (IoU = 0.9190131). Audit-component ablation attributes the observed reduction in IoU-degrading outputs to the train-learned risk veto, while LLM review serves as a selective, structured, and auditable assistive interface rather than an independently validated source of automatic improvement. These results position AgenticInspect as a risk-aware inspection framework that converts static segmentation outputs into auditable refinement decisions.

items.title: AI Agent Lifecycle Governance Framework
items.abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed as persistent digital actors that can reason, access enterprise knowledge, invoke tools, and execute business actions. Unlike conventional applications, agents may adapt their behavior dynamically and operate with varying levels of autonomy, making lifecycle governance essential. This paper proposes an AI Agent Lifecycle Governance Framework covering ideation, risk classification, design, data and model selection, identity, tool approval, development, testing, security review, Responsible AI evaluation, deployment, runtime monitoring, change management, recertification, suspension, and retirement. The framework integrates enterprise architecture, model risk management, cybersecurity, auditability, human oversight, and operational governance into a repeatable lifecycle. It defines governance gates, accountable roles, evidence requirements, runtime controls, and measurable KPIs/KRIs. The proposed approach enables enterprises to scale agentic AI responsibly while maintaining traceability, bounded authority, regulatory readiness, and long-term operational control.

items.title: AI and Data-Driven Decision Making: Innovating Strategy in Modern Business Management
items.abstract: Advanced AI technologies and analytics inform critical decisions within contemporary corporate strategies. Existing research underscores the advantages of using artificial intelligence for operations and analysis but lacks comprehensive insights into how these systems affect overall strategy formulation, business flexibility, and leadership performance in various sectors. In pursuit of filling this void, our current research investigates how machine learning, predictive analysis, natural language handling, and automated systems contribute significantly to improving business strategies. This analysis explores how companies utilize vast amounts of information to predict changes in markets, enhance their processes, elevate service quality for customers, and secure an edge over rivals. Drawing upon examples from sectors like retail, health care, manufacturing, and finance, this document demonstrates how artificial intelligence enhances business strategies through real-world applications. Additionally, this research examines significant obstacles including issues related to personal information security, discrimination in machine learning models, moral considerations, and the necessity of efficient cooperation between humans and artificial intelligence systems. Evidence highlights the significance of cultivating data-centric environments, enhancing technological frameworks, and nurturing leaders adept at guiding AI-informed organizational shifts. In summary, this study offers a comprehensive view of how artificial intelligence and digital ecosystems facilitate agile, robust, and insightful approaches within evolving corporate landscapes.

items.title: AI as a Catalyst for Purpose-Driven Business
items.abstract: Chapter 7 explores how artificial intelligence is transforming the architecture, culture and governance of modern organisations, revealing both the risks and opportunities of technological acceleration. It argues that AI does not simply automate existing processes but fundamentally reshapes how work is organised, how decisions are made and how value is created. Drawing on the author’s experience redesigning an advisory organisation at Human Planet, the chapter illustrates how AI can invert traditional hierarchical structures, replacing labour-intensive pyramids with lean, purpose-driven systems where experienced professionals are supported by intelligent tools. In this model, technology handles complexity and repetition, while humans focus on judgement, creativity and service. Beyond structural efficiency, the chapter examines the cultural and ethical implications of AI adoption. It highlights how intelligent systems can restore human-centred productivity by removing administrative burdens, enabling organisations to redirect energy towards meaning, collaboration and innovation. At the same time, the chapter warns that AI amplifies the values embedded in an organisation: when guided by vocation and ethical leadership, it strengthens transparency, accountability and stakeholder empowerment; when misaligned, it risks accelerating bias, opacity and institutional failure. Ultimately, Chapter 7 positions artificial intelligence not as a substitute for purpose but as a catalyst that makes organisational vocation more actionable, reinforcing the central premise of the vocating framework: that technology must serve human dignity, long-term stewardship and meaningful contribution.
