items.title: AI for Everyone: Designing an Introductory AI Course Across Disciplines
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence reshapes virtually every field, universities face a growing imperative to ensure AI literacy is not reserved for computer science majors alone. This panel presents the collaborative design of an introductory AI course built for undergraduate general education — one that serves students across disciplines, regardless of technical background. Two co-designers will share the story of building the course from complementary angles. The first presenter will address the technical foundation of the curriculum: how core AI concepts such as machine learning, data, and algorithms were translated into accessible, hands-on learning experiences for non-specialist students. The second presenter will explore the philosophical framework woven throughout the course — examining questions of ethics, agency, bias, and what it means to be human in an age of intelligent machines. The panelists will discuss how technical and philosophical threads were intentionally integrated rather than siloed, creating a course where students not only understand how AI works, but are equipped to think critically about why it matters. Attendees will come away with practical insights on curriculum structure, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and strategies for making AI education inclusive for students from diverse academic and experiential backgrounds. This session is designed for faculty, instructional designers, and administrators interested in developing or expanding AI literacy offerings at their institutions.

items.title: AI for Grading from the Teaching Perspective (with an EssayGrader Case Comparison)
items.abstract: AI has taken the academic world by storm, dramatically affecting written assignments and student performance evaluations. This paper examines the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) from the teaching perspective, with emphasis on daily grading workflows. We analyze benefits such as fair and consistent application of rubrics, the ability to incorporate articles and course materials as inputs to grading, and the delivery of individualized, extensive feedback. We compare these capabilities against a representative product—EssayGrader—situate our claims within current scholarship on Automated Essay Scoring (AES) and Large Language Models (LLMs) as graders, and provide policy guidance.

This paper offers a thorough analysis of the changing dynamics of AI in education, focusing on personalized learning and educational technology. This synthesis of current research and trends seeks to inform future advancements in the evolving symbiosis between AI and education, promoting a knowledgeable and progressive approach to AI integration in the educational domain.

items.title: AI in PRACTICE
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed in healthcare. Radiology is one of the most active areas of clinical AI development. Despite substantial investments, many AI systems struggle to gain traction in clinical practice. The issues are rarely purely technical; they concern how AI tools fit into existing workflows, how they interact with professional responsibilities, and how they sit within institutional arrangements. It also remains unclear how core values in AI research such as explainability, value alignment, accountability, and trust are negotiated in clinical work. Established Health Technology Assessment (HTA) models define assessment domains but offer limited guidance on implementation: how technologies are staged within workflows, how responsibilities are redistributed, and how local conditions redefine value for different stakeholders. This paper presents the AI in PRACTICE framework, a five-phase methodology grounded in Techno-Anthropology and its relational ontology, for examining the situated work through which AI becomes part of clinical practice. Explainability, value alignment, trust, and distributed responsibility are understood as produced through socio-technical practices. The framework complements existing HTA models through iterative engagement and stakeholder participation. Insights are illustrated through three radiology-facing AI projects showing how assessment criteria are enacted, resisted, and revised in context, and how the framework generates practice-based artefacts.

items.title: AI in Sustainable Finance: A Study on Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Funds Investment Patterns Around the World
items.abstract: The proposed research centres on how artificial intelligence (AI) influences the choice of capital by foreign investors in ESG-related funds. It compares thirty funds across different regions using AI methods and traditional ESG funds. The results suggest that AI-based funds utilising machine learning and natural language processing show better financial results and stable risk-adjusted performance. Moreover, these technologies improve the quality of ESG disclosures and help detect inconsistencies, serving as a useful indicator of greenwashing cases. Regression analyses demonstrate a positive relationship between AI use and final fund performance. Great regional differences exist, with North America showing the highest integration. AI makes ESG investing more transparent and efficient, though regulatory frameworks are required.

items.title: AI literacy: Gen Z expectations vs. organisational practices in India's dynamic job market
items.abstract: The mismatch between Generation Z's (Gen Z) high expectations of artificial intelligence (AI) and organisational AI practices has profound implications for vocational well-being in India's job market. This research explores the structural path between Gen Z’s AI Expectations, Organisational AI Practices, and AI Literacy-Driven Vocational Well-being, with Skills Velocity as a key contextual variable in a rapidly changing, technology-driven landscape.This research used a mixed-methods approach. A structured questionnaire was administered to 203 Gen Z professionals and HR managers in AI-heavy industries (IT, BFSI and manufacturing) in Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities in India. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) using the lavaan package in R was used to test the path model. We triangulated our findings with 20 semi-structured interviews. The sample was skewed towards males (70:30 male-to-female) and non-normal.Based on the findings, the model fit was satisfactory. Gen Z's AI Expectations positively impacted Organisational AI Practices (β = 0.608, p < .001) and AI Literacy-driven Vocational Well-being (β = 0.449, p < .001). Organisational AI Practices also significantly and positively influenced Vocational Well-being (β = 0.418, p < .001). The variance in Organisational AI Practices and Vocational Well-being explained by the model was 36.9% and 60.4%, respectively.The research suggests that matching organisational AI practices to Gen Z expectations is crucial to improving AI literacy-based vocational well-being in India's ever-evolving labour market. The findings reveal the important role of Gen Z as a driver for change in organisations and the need for forward-looking, skills-velocity-sensitive human resource management strategies such as AI upskilling and training, ethical AI policies and lifelong learning opportunities to enhance retention and workforce preparedness.

items.title: AI sycophancy, self-interpretation, and conversational contentment
items.abstract: Abstract AI sycophancy is often conceptualized as a chatbot’s tendency to flout truth, accuracy, or other epistemic standards to shield users from hurt feelings, or otherwise protect them from the consequences of their thoughts, words, or actions. In this paper, I argue against this conception. That is, I argue that sycophantic AI behavior does not necessarily aim to protect users, nor that its harms are essentially epistemic . There are highly prevalent cases in which sycophantic AI chatbots actively contribute to their users’ knowledge. One class of such examples involves cases in which chatbots are used as auto-hermeneutic technologies —as tools to facilitate the user’s interpretation of her own cares, concerns, values, and other identity components and life events. In these cases, LLMs can help articulate the user’s avowed self-interpretations. In turn, avowals of these interpretations by users can often have downstream effects that render the interpretations true. If this is correct, then LLMs can often advance the user’s knowledge regarding important truths about herself. Simultaneously, as I explain, interpretations offered by LLMs may be deeply harmful. This understanding of AI sycophancy can help us clarify what is so disturbing about it, as well as resist the temptation to draw too tight an analogy between sycophantic behaviors in AI systems and in humans.

items.title: AI Tools and EFL Identity: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Gender and Cultural Representation in AI-Generated Reading Materials for Gulf University Students
items.abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom has revolutionized the production of teaching content. However, the ideological implications of AI-generated content have been markedly under-researched in non-Western contexts. This study employs Fairclough’s three-dimensional framework of Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) on a corpus of 45 AI-generated EFL reading texts produced by the ChatGPT-4o, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Microsoft Copilot in response to five standardized instructional prompts. It aims to investigate how gender and Arab cultural identity is discursively constructed in materials targeting Gulf university EFL learners. Analysis of the findings show that the female professional is consistently represented through discourse of relational and communal achievement while the single male professional is coded through individual enterprise and resilience. Leadership discourse universalizes the individual while entirely erasing gender and cultural identity across the nine texts. Furthermore, a Western nuclear family development narrative renders the Arab family invisible. Finally, Microsoft Copilot shows the lowest cultural specificity and the highest degree of textual cloning across platforms. The findings further affirm that L2 writing created by these AI models replicates Western liberal ideological formations, thus marginalizing the cultural and gender identities of the Arab learners. The research makes pedagogical, technological, and policy recommendations for the culturally responsive use of AI tools in higher education in the Gulf.

items.title: AI Tutors, Worksheets, and Task Design: Matching AI Tools to Learning Structure
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used by students as a learning resource in STEM courses. However, classroom observations and survey data suggest that unstructured AI use may correlate with reduced student achievement. Two concerns are especially relevant: AI systems can produce incorrect responses in tasks requiring precise validation, and students may use AI in ways that reduce active engagement with course material. This session presents two instructional approaches designed to address these limitations: structured AI-generated worksheets and in-chat AI tutors. AI worksheets generate controlled sets of practice problems within instructor-defined course constraints. In-chat tutors provide interactive practice through problem generation, Socratic questioning, and feedback-driven guidance. The usefulness of each approach depends on the structure of the learning task. Drawing from iterative development and testing primarily in introductory chemistry, we examine four types of tasks: (1) conceptual and explanatory, (2) structured tasks with low ambiguity, (3) multi-step quantitative tasks, and (4) highly deterministic symbolic or structural tasks. Examples from chemical nomenclature, dimensional analysis, stoichiometry, Lewis structures, laboratory writing, and mathematical validation illustrate where different AI approaches worked reliably—and where they did not. Participants will receive ready-to-use prompts for both AI worksheet systems and in-chat tutors, along with implementation strategies and observed limitations. The session concludes with a practical framework for selecting AI tools based on the structure of the learning task rather than disciplinary content alone.

items.title: AI Workforce Governance Framework
items.abstract: AI agents are becoming a new category of enterprise workforce alongside employees, contractors, softwarerobots, and traditional applications. As organizations assign AI systems persistent responsibilities, access rights, service expectations, and decision authority, workforce governance must expand beyond human resource management and technology operations. This paper proposes an AI Workforce Governance Framework that defines how enterprises should classify digital workers, assign ownership, establish roles and decision rights, manage identity and access, define supervision models, measure performance, control risk, govern collaboration with humans, and retire AI workforce components. The framework integrates enterprise architecture, operating model design, cybersecurity, Responsible AI, process governance, workforce transformation, and portfolio management. It enables organizations to treat AI agents as governed digital roles rather than uncontrolled automation, supporting productivity and innovation while maintaining accountability, transparency, human authority, and organizational resilience

items.title: AI-Agent-Based Web Application Security Testing vs. Conventional Automated Security Testing: An Exploratory Case Study
items.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) and agent-based architectures have introduced new possibilities for automating web application security testing. Unlike traditional vulnerability scanners that rely mainly on signature-based detection, LLM-powered agents can analyze application context and dynamically adapt testing strategies. This exploratory case study examined two specific laboratory-defined workflows for identifying web application security weaknesses: a human-supervised agent-based workflow and a conventional vulnerability scanner workflow. The evaluation was performed in a controlled laboratory environment against the same target application and predefined ground truth, while each workflow retained its respective application-access, discovery, and authentication mechanisms. The agent-based framework was developed using Claude Code, the Model Context Protocol, and Burp Suite Professional, while the scanner-based approach utilized Qualys Web Application Scanning. Results were mapped to a predefined ground truth covering SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting, and Broken Access Control and reported using Recall, Precision, and false-positive counts where estimable. The findings describe what each completed workflow showed under the tested conditions, including coverage, tester effort, and validation workload, and outline directions for further evaluation.

items.title: AI-Aware Student Recommendations for GenAI in Higher Ed
items.abstract: What do well-informed students say about the use and integration of AI in their college educations? In Spring and Summer 2026 semesters, students in three sections of ENG 102 at UNR wrote AI-aware white papers with policy recommendations for the integration of genAI into higher education. To develop white paper policies, students read a variety of scholarly, public, and popular sources that show a variety of perspectives on Generative AI and LLMs, including the environmental and cognitive impacts. Then they considered the values and concerns of their audiences—peers, professors, and/or university administrators—to propose “sensible, well-informed, and well-reasoned” policies. This session will discuss their recommendations, insights, and the somewhat surprising classroom experience of teaching sustained, critical enquiry about Generative AI.

items.title: AI-Based Decision-Making Framework for Climate Change-Induced Flood Risk Management and Urban Resilience
items.abstract: Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of urban flooding, creating unprecedented challenges for municipalities worldwide. This study develops an AI-based decision-making framework that integrates machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and geospatial analytics to enhance urban flood risk management and resilience planning. The framework employs ensemble machine learning algorithms including Random Forest, XG Boost, and Cat Boost for flood susceptibility mapping, coupled with SHAP-based interpretability to decode model predictions and translate them into actionable policy insights at administrative scales. A city-scale digital twin component enables real-time flood impact simulation and cascading infrastructure disruption analysis, while a multi-criteria decision support module prioritizes adaptation investments based on economic risk assessment and equity considerations. The framework was validated using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR data and hydrological records across diverse urban environments, demonstrating superior predictive performance with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values exceeding 0.95 for ensemble models. Results reveal that elevation, proximity to hydrological features, and impervious surface density consistently emerge as dominant flood drivers, with their relative importance varying significantly across districts. The decision support system successfully transformed pixel-level predictions into ward-level actionable recommendations, enabling evidence-based zoning, drainage infrastructure prioritization, and targeted nature-based solutions deployment. The framework addresses critical gaps in explainability, scalability, and policy relevance that have limited the operational adoption of AI in urban flood governance. The study concludes that integrating AI-driven analytics with participatory decision-making processes can substantially enhance adaptive capacity in flood-prone urban systems, though algorithmic transparency, data equity, and institutional readiness remain essential preconditions for equitable implementation.

items.title: AI-Based Early Prediction of Iron-Deficiency Anemia in Rural Women
items.abstract: Anemia is a common disease that may occur in individuals due to low levels of hemoglobin in the blood, whereas conventional diagnosis usually requires clinical examination and laboratory tests. Preliminary screening is often hindered by economic, availability, and even early recognition challenges. AnemiaVision is the proposed artificial intelligence system designed to recognize potential cases of anemia from conjunctiva images. AnemiaVision uses a Convolutional Neural Network to process and classify the image data into anemic and non-anemic classes. The model was trained using a dataset of conjunctiva images categorized into Anemic and Non-Anemic classes. The images were preprocessed and normalized before model training. AnemiaVision is comprised of the trained model and a web interface, which allows users to upload a conjunctiva image and receive screening results with model confidence. The system was implemented using Python programming language, TensorFlow/Keras framework, OpenCV computer vision library, and PHP web interface framework. The proposed system was experimentally evaluated, and results showed potential for rapid preliminary screening of anemia. AnemiaVision is proposed as an educational and screening tool, which cannot substitute laboratory tests and clinical diagnosis by medical professionals.

items.title: AI-Based Optimization Models for High-Performance Computing and Intelligent Network Architectures
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a necessary technology to optimize High-Performance computers (HPC) systems and intelligent network architecture, such as optimizing the use of resources, the schedulization of workloads and network efficiency. This paper discusses how the three AI-based optimization tools, i.e., Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) can be optimized to enhance performance in the HPC environment. It was done using a quantitative, simulation based, approach on the benchmark HPC workload and HPC network datasets. Data cleaning, feature selection, normalization and train-test splitting were used to preprocess the datasets and then model implementation and evaluation took place. The models were evaluated based on performance such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, execution time, resource consumption, throughput, latency as well as the energy consumption. Experimental results demonstrated that the DRL model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 96.8, 93.8 CPU resources consumption, 96.1 network efficiency, 12.8 Gbps throughput and 5.3 ms (lowest) network latency values. LSTM had the highest prediction accuracy of 95.2, and XGBoost had a score of 93.9 with the lowest training time rate of 39 minutes. The findings indicate that AI-based optimization is tremendously more effective regarding calculations and adaptability, scheduling, and resource allocation compared to the conventional ones. The suggested framework offers a viable solution to scalable, smart and energy efficient, intelligent HPC systems, which can be used to support next generations of computing and networking systems.

items.abstract: The proposed work develops a cost-effective IoT and artificial-intelligence-based predictive maintenance system for electric motor fault detection. A BO geared DC motor is monitored using an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with DHT11, INA219, and MPU9250 sensors to measure temperature, current, voltage, and vibration parameters. The collected sensor data are processed using time-domain statistical features and transmitted through Wi-Fi to a local server for analysis. Machine learning models, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost, are employed and combined using a soft-voting approach to improve fault classification. The system categorizes the motor condition into normal, highcurrent, and maintenance-required states. In addition, vibration, current, and temperature trends are analyzed to provide early warnings before critical thresholds are reached. Blynk IoT is used for remote monitoring, while automatic email notifications are generated when abnormal conditions persist. The study demonstrates the feasibility of implementing an affordable real-time predictive maintenance solution suitable for laboratories, small industries, and academic applications.

When artificial intelligence (AI) is embedded within the twin, the resulting system can move beyond visualization to support fault identification, anomaly detection, degradation assessment, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, and maintenance decision-making. items.title: AI-Driven Next-Generation DDoS Mitigation in IoT: A Comprehensive Survey of Deep Learning and Large Language Models
items.abstract: The global Internet of Things (IoT) network has experienced unprecedented expansion, reaching 75.44 billion connected devices worldwide. Due to this rapid growth, the IoT ecosystem has become larger but also more vulnerable to various threats in cyberspace. As a result, this situation has accelerated the development of more complex cyberattacks, especially Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, which can damage systems by overwhelming network traffic. This attack exploits the inherent vulnerabilities of IoT networks with limited resources, leading to significant service interruptions, monetary losses, and potentially the failure of vital infrastructures. As a result, this survey presents a new taxonomy of attack types, a thorough assessment of conventional and AI-driven detection techniques, and a comparison of advanced countermeasures. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive and systematic overview of DDoS attack detection, prevention, and mitigation approaches for the IoT. A major contribution of this work is the inclusion of blockchain-based security frameworks, federated learning, deep learning, machine learning, and quantum computing paradigms in its discussion for reducing DDoS attacks on the IoT. Furthermore, real-world case studies highlight the severe impact of such attacks on mission-critical domains, including smart cities, healthcare, and industrial control systems (ICSs). This survey provides a basis for cybersecurity researchers, security experts, and hobbyists, grounded in the understanding gained from previous research.

items.title: AI-Driven Personalised Learning: Global Trends, Transformations, and Ethical Imperatives in Education
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming education by enabling personalized learning pathways, automating tasks, and creating interactive technologies that expand access. Recent reports show that 87% of schools worldwide have adopted AI tools in some form, and the AI-in-education market is projected to grow from $5.88 billion in 2024 to $32.3 billion by 2030 ( Grand View Research, 2025 ; SQ Magazine, 2025 ). This review highlights how AI enhances individualized learning, improves student engagement, and streamlines administration. Simultaneously, challenges such as privacy risks, algorithmic bias, and the digital divide remain. Global frameworks from UNESCO emphasize that without strong ethical policies, AI can deepen inequalities rather than reduce them. This paper adopted a structural literature review approach that synthesized global reports, peer-reviewed studies, and policy documents to map out current trends. The paper concludes that AI&s;s potential in education can be realized only through responsible adoption, professional development for educators, and inclusive infrastructure investments. This paper integrates global adoption statistics with ethical and equity perspectives, highlighting the research gap in empirical classroom-based studies. These implications suggest that policymakers and educators must balance innovation with safeguards to ensure equitable outcomes.

items.title: AI-Driven Personalization in Digital Marketing: Consumer Trust, Engagement, and Purchase Behavior - A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization has increasingly transformed digital marketing by enabling firms to deliver individualized recommendations, content, and offers based on consumer data and behavioral patterns. However, the growing use of personalization also raises important questions regarding consumer trust, engagement, and purchase behavior. This study aims to conduct a systematic literature review (SLR) of research on AI-driven personalization in digital marketing to examine its implications for consumer trust, engagement, and purchase behavior. Using Scopus as the primary database, the search process identified 2,906 records and, through successive filtering and screening procedures, resulted in 51 eligible studies. Bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and thematic synthesis were employed to identify publication trends, intellectual structures, and key research themes. The findings indicate a shift from technology-oriented research toward consumer-centered perspectives, with increasing attention to consumer experience, trust, engagement, privacy, transparency, purchase intention, and purchase behavior. The review further demonstrates that the effectiveness of AI-driven personalization is context-dependent and influenced by consumer perceptions and data-related concerns. These findings provide an integrated basis for understanding the evolving role of AI personalization in contemporary digital marketing

items.title: AI-driven whole-life costing for decision-ready UK public building retrofits
items.abstract: Abstract Public-sector building retrofits in the United Kingdom require decisions that balance whole-life cost, carbon reduction, service continuity and auditability under limited data and constrained capital budgets. This paper develops a decision-ready whole-life costing (WLC) workflow that integrates environmental, social and governance (ESG) priorities with uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence (AI) for public-building retrofit appraisal. The workflow combines national non-domestic Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) and Display Energy Certificate (DEC) data, Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme (PSDS) delivery evidence and stakeholder inputs to construct a scenario library of public-building archetypes, retrofit actions and appraisal constraints. Stakeholder priorities from interviews, a questionnaire and a co-design workshop are translated into transparent weights using fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (F-AHP). These weights parameterise a reinforcement learning (RL) planner, while a Bayesian convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (BCNN–LSTM) surrogate provides uncertainty-bounded energy, carbon and cost trajectories for repeated policy evaluation. Results show that the workflow supports auditable retrofit sequencing across archetype and budget conditions and improves composite ESG performance relative to conventional WLC-only, £/tCO 2 e and static multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) baselines. For 1000 matched archetype–budget cases, the trained deep Q-network (DQN) decision-search stage achieves a 30.03-fold speedup over traditional scalar feasible-sequence enumeration. The contribution is an integrated and explainable WLC–ESG–AI workflow for early-stage public retrofit decision support. The current validation remains based on public datasets and scenario-level evidence so future work should extend the framework using project-specific metered data, digital twins and live portfolio deployment.

items.title: AI-Enabled Financial Phishing and the Digital Literacy Deficit Protecting Student and Young Learner Data
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has structurally transformed financial phishing, collapsing the cost of personalised attacks; India recorded 135,173 financial phishing attacks in H1 2024, a 175% rise over 2023. This chapter examines the convergence of AI-enabled phishing, student data vulnerability, and digital literacy deficits in India's skill-based educational institutions (ITIs, polytechnics, skill universities), a population absent from existing cybersecurity literature despite holding data regulated under the DPDP Act, 2023. Drawing on Routine Activity Theory, Protection Motivation Theory, the Digital Literacy Continuum, and Institutional Theory, it develops the Protection Gap construct and a Four-Layer Institutional Defence Model. A primary survey (N = 96, seven states) finds 66.7% encountered suspected phishing, mostly via WhatsApp; only 25.0% identified a genuine message; 59.4% were unaware of the DPDP Act; and 43.8% reported no explicit consent for Aadhaar/bank data. The chapter closes with recommendations for MeitY, AICTE, NSDC, and the Data Protection Board of India.

items.title: AI-Enabled Wearable Sensor Technologies for Athlete Performance Monitoring: A Critical Review of Signal Processing, Machine Learning, and Real-Time Embedded Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Wearable sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly being used to quantify athlete movement, physiological response, training load, and recovery in field and laboratory settings. However, the practical value of these systems depends not only on the predictive capability of an algorithm but also on sensor validity, signal quality, hardware constraints, real-time processing, and the transferability of models across athletes and sports. This review examines the technical pipeline linking wearable electronic sensors to athlete-monitoring decisions, with particular attention to inertial measurement units, global navigation satellite systems, photoplethysmography, electrocardiography, electromyography, pressure sensing, and multimodal systems. It synthesizes evidence on signal conditioning, segmentation, feature engineering, classical machine learning, deep learning, sensor fusion, edge inference, and embedded implementation. Existing reviews indicate that wearable devices can support useful monitoring, but accuracy varies by metric, device, movement pattern, and validation setting; performance under controlled conditions should not be assumed to generalize to competition. Key challenges include motion artifacts, inconsistent protocols, small and imbalanced datasets, leakage between training and test sets, limited external validation, battery and communication constraints, privacy, and unclear decision thresholds. The review proposes a layered reference architecture and a validation framework that links engineering performance to sport-specific usefulness. Future research should prioritize synchronized multimodal datasets, athlete-independent testing, interpretable and uncertainty-aware models, energy-efficient edge AI, secure data governance, and transparent reporting. The article’s contribution is an engineering-oriented synthesis that connects sensor physics and embedded constraints with the needs of physical education and sports science. items.title: AI-Generated Deepfakes and Trust in Digital Communication in Namibia
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated the development of deepfake technology, enabling the creation of highly realistic fabricated audio, video, and visual content that closely resembles authentic media. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining an online survey of 47 Namibian internet users and a total of 12 key informants were interviewed. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data were subjected to thematic analysis. The findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on deepfake technologies by providing empirical evidence from Namibia and offering practical recommendations for enhancing digital literacy, strengthening regulatory frameworks, and improving institutional preparedness.

items.title: AI-Guided Clinical Image Interpretation System for Precision Treatment Planning
items.abstract: Radiological examinations increasingly leverage artificial intelligence to enhance diagnostic performance by compensating for expertise shortages, particularly in specialized interpretation. Despite academic AI models achieving compelling accuracy, adoption remains low. An objective, evidence-based examination of AI-guided clinical image interpretation seeks to expose the underlying reasons. The primary challenge lies not in accuracy but in fully automated analysis, especially for multimodal and multidimensional datasets. Introduction of uncertainty measures, image explainability, and real-world data reduce recognition to a decisive-supporting role—helping radiologists to detect previously unnoticed abnormalities—or even to precautionary analysis. Patients requesting precision medicine and therapy planning—and those at high risk of neglected pathology—stand to gain the greatest benefit. Relevant AI architecture considers imaging cues suitable for precision medicine or requiring additional methods to obtain interpretable images. Successful performance testing against an external, hidden reference dataset promotes vital user trust. Machine learning achieves best results where all potentially pathological abnormalities are identified and their presence virtually guaranteed, as in multi-class recognition. Data scarcity, however, impedes clinically relevant solutions. Explainability, essential for medical applications and clinical acceptance, extends simply beyond clinical decision support to provide saliency maps and, better still, clinically meaningful image regions or qualities. Attention maps may even bring a form of rule-based reasoning within reach. Clinical integration that reproduces the technical conditions under which model diagnostic measures are calculated raises the challenge of uncertainty quantification—a necessary condition for clinical decision support. Convolutional neural networks trained for photo-quality classification, par excellence supervised image quality assessment, provide the basic cues for uncertainty quantification. Imaging acquisition, modality, and systems are also defined in terms of current PACS/EPIC systems. PE, pre-symptomatic examination or precautionary examination, is defined as a patient-user group prepared to cover the cost of an examination with lower diagnostic accuracy and a high level of uncertainty.

items.abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) based robo-advisor has become a disruptive game-changer in the field of investment advisory service, altering the manner in which portfolios are managed as well as how individuals are making investing choices. These platforms provide cost-efficient, personalized and scalable financial recommendations using Big data analytics, machine learning, and algorithmic automation. The paper is a systematic literature review carried out with the help of PRISMA to draw generalizations on the available literature on the topic of AI-powered robo-advisors, the basics behind their technology, the impact on investor behavior, the performance of their portfolios, and the ethical and regulatory issues related to this field. Based on the searches of peer-reviewed published literature published in 2016-2025, the review determines the main themes in the context of decision accuracy, reduction of behavioral bias, risk optimization, and democratization of financial advice. The results reveal that the efficiency and objectiveness of investment management is considerably increased by robo-advisors, but the issues of data privacy, algorithmic transparency, and regulation are raised. The paper concludes that hybrid advisory models that integrate AI with the human judgment skills are the most sustainable future of the investment advisory services. New issues of data privacy, algorithmic transparency, ethical fairness, and regulatory compliance are critically looked into as well as those benefits such as automation, objectivity, accessibility and democratization of financial advice are identified. It argues in the study that hybrid models of advising that integrate AI capabilities with human decision-making will probably Explain the future of the investment guidance services utilising real case studies and research that is currently available.

items.title: AI‐Supported Research‐Led Teaching in Syntegrative Project‐Based Learning: Educator Questioning, Feedback, and Student Learning Outcomes in Authentic Industry Projects
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new possibilities for connecting research‐led teaching with authentic industry projects, yet its educational value depends on how educators organize inquiry rather than on technological use alone. This study examined the relationships among AI‐supported research‐led teaching (AIRLT), educator questioning (EQ), educator feedback (EF), student inquiry engagement (SIE), and authentic project learning outcomes (APLO) within Syntegrative Project‐Based Learning. A quantitative cross‐sectional survey was conducted with 898 undergraduate students from 12 universities in Vietnam who had participated in authentic industry or organizational projects involving AI‐supported inquiry and educator guidance. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) showed that AIRLT was positively associated with EQ ( β = 0.642) and EF ( β = 0.611). Both EQ ( β = 0.463) and EF ( β = 0.349) were positively associated with SIE, which, in turn, showed a strong positive association with APLO ( β = 0.689). All six specific indirect effects were significant, indicating statistically significant indirect associations among AI‐supported teaching, educator guidance, student inquiry, and perceived authentic learning outcomes. The findings contribute an educator‐mediated perspective to Syntegrative Education by showing that AI is most educationally meaningful when embedded in purposeful questioning, feedback, and sustained student inquiry. The study highlights the importance of designing AI‐supported industry projects around evidence evaluation, iterative feedback, reflection, and active investigation of authentic problems rather than treating AI use as an educational objective in itself.

items.title: Algorithmic Provenance: When and Why Consumers Discount Products Made With AI ‐Involved Processes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Firms increasingly incorporate generative and non‐generative artificial intelligence (AI) into product design, formulation, and production, and they face a disclosure question: how should they describe the role of AI to consumers? Across six studies, including analysis of 1800 marketplace listings and five pre‐registered experiments (total experimental N = 2760), we introduce and test a 2‐by‐2 framework of algorithmic provenance defined by the AI's role (agentic vs. assistive) and its visibility in the final product (visible vs. invisible). Identical products are evaluated differently depending on where they fall in this taxonomy. Agentic AI involvement (AI as designer) reduces consumer product attitudes, perceived quality, purchase intentions, and willingness to pay relative to assistive AI involvement (AI as a tool for a human designer). The effect is amplified when AI involvement is visible in the final product. The downstream responses are partially mediated by a new construct, perceived authenticity of creative intention, which captures consumers' inference about whether a human creator pursued a genuine creative vision. The effect is larger for expressive than for functional product domains and larger among consumers primed to hold an independent self‐construal. A scalable managerial intervention, creative‐intent framing, narrows the agentic penalty by approximately half, again through the authenticity mechanism. The findings identify a substantively important new construct for AI disclosure research, refine theories of algorithmic aversion, and offer marketers an actionable disclosure design principle.

items.title: An adaptive congestion-aware graph neural routing framework with hybrid microcoded event-driven control for network-on-chip systems
items.abstract: Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures have become a fundamental communication backbone for many-core processors, artificial intelligence accelerators, edge-computing platforms, and high-performance embedded systems. However, achieving efficient packet routing in large-scale NoCs remains challenging due to dynamic traffic variations, congestion propagation, limited global network visibility, and stringent hardware constraints. Conventional deterministic and heuristic routing algorithms suffer from reduced adaptability under non-uniform traffic conditions, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based routers primarily rely on local state representations and finite-state-machine (FSM) controllers, limiting their scalability, topology awareness, and hardware deployability. To address these limitations, this work proposes an Adaptive Congestion-Aware Graph Neural Routing Framework with Hybrid Microcoded Event-Driven Control for Network-on-Chip Systems. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components: (i) an Adaptive Congestion-Aware Graph Neural Network (ACA-GNN) encoder that generates compact topology-aware embeddings by capturing local and multi-hop congestion dependencies through congestion-aware message propagation, (ii) a quantized Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent that performs low-latency adaptive routing decisions using compact graph embeddings, and (iii) a Hybrid Microcoded Event-Driven Controller (H-µEDC) that replaces conventional FSM-based control with programmable event-triggered micro-routines to ensure deterministic routing execution. The proposed architecture is implemented on a Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA and evaluated using BookSim2 cycle-accurate simulation, Orion 3.0 power modeling, synthetic traffic patterns, and PARSEC/Rodinia benchmark workloads. Experimental results demonstrate up to 48% lower packet latency, and 31% lower energy per flit compared with state-of-the-art heuristic and machine-learning-based routing approaches. Hardware implementation further requires only 1.2% LUTs, 1.4% flip-flops, three DSP blocks, one BRAM, and 0.556 W power consumption while maintaining deterministic single-cycle routing decisions using cached ACA-GNN embeddings. These results demonstrate that the proposed ACA-GNN-HµEDC framework effectively combines topology-aware routing intelligence, congestion adaptivity, hardware efficiency, and scalability, making it a practical solution for next-generation many-core Network-on-Chip systems.

items.title: An AI-interpretable multidimensional intelligence-driven framework for student performance prediction using local LLM-based narrative reasoning
items.abstract: Predicting student performance has become a vital objective in educational data mining, however existing models remain limited by limited feature sets, opaque decision processes, and the absence of real-time, context-aware interpretative intelligence. This study presents a novel hybrid Artificial Intelligence (AI) architecture that integrates cognitive, emotional, and general intelligence indicators with formative assessment/class performance data to construct a multidimensional demonstration of student performance. The system utilizes a mathematically formalized feature-weighting mechanism that allows domain experts to regulate the influence of key predictors prior to training, enabling a tunable and educator-configurable modeling process. Interaction between cognitive, emotional, and behavioral properties are explicitly engineered to capture complex effects often overlooked in prior research. An ensemble predictive model combining Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, and Linear Regression is used to predict student grades, with uncertainty measured through variance-based confidence intervals. The integrated system exhibited strong predictive capability, attaining high accuracy (R 2 = 0.9014, 95% CI [0.8882, 0.9121], 10,000 bootstrap resamples) with low prediction error, confirming the stability and reliability of the ensemble model. Understanding why a model produces a particular prediction is often as important as the prediction itself. To address the interpretability gap, the system incorporates SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based global and local explanations, a counterfactual simulation engine that estimates the marginal impact of improving specific attributes, and a local generative AI layer deployed via Ollama that creates these outputs into structured, real-time narrative feedback. Running the Large Language Model (LLM) locally ensures privacy-preserving, institution-compliant interpretability while permitting interactive, student specific explanations. This integration of predictive modeling, explainability, simulation, and local generative reasoning creates a unified decision-support framework that exceeds traditional black-box approaches. Experimental assessment shows that the model not only achieves viable predictive accuracy but also provides actionable insights into feature influence, model stability, and potential intervention pathways.

items.title: An All‐Fabric Wearable System for Human‐Machine Interaction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable human–machine interfaces (HMIs) are at the forefront of next‐generation intelligent systems, demanding interfaces that are not only accurate and responsive, but also ergonomic, stretchable, and seamlessly integrated into daily life. In this work, we present a novel HMI system enabled by a glove and garment, based on fully textile, matrix‐free capacitive strain sensors (CSSs). Our sensor is fabricated via a single‐step, sewing‐machine‐compatible double‐twisted knitting process of silver‐coated knitted textile electrodes and a nylon/elastane textile dielectric, eliminating the need for post‐processing, polymer encapsulation, or rigid substrates. The resulting all‐fabric CSS demonstrates a high gauge factor of 2.03 over a broad strain range (0–72%), with excellent linearity (R 2 = 0.982), hysteresis (7.80%), and minimal signal creep. The textile‐based architecture preserves garment‐level wearability, with the nylon/elastane dielectric exhibiting a porosity of ∼66%, while the silver‐coated textile electrode (∼77% porosity) maintains a low and stable resistance (∼4.4 Ω) under 0–60% strain. Integrated into a wearable glove, the proposed system enables detection of 10 distinct hand gestures with recognition accuracy of 90.5%. This work marks a significant advancement toward fully textile‐integrated, breathable, comfortable, stretchable, and high‐performance HMI solutions, with broad implications for virtual environments, assistive technologies, and next‐generation wearable robotics.

items.title: Analysis of China's new materials industry landscape and corporate strategic planning
items.abstract: The new materials industry is a strategic pillar industry underpinning China's pursuit of technological self-reliance and self-strengthening. It plays a vital role in the development of advanced manufacturing, the achievement of the "dual carbon" goals, and the security of industrial and supply chains. The deep integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with materials Research and Development (R&D) is continuously reshaping the innovation and production models of the industry. Existing literature has extensively examined new materials technologies and AI-driven innovation, but relatively little research has systematically analyzed the competitive landscape of the industry from the perspective of industrial economics. Clarifying the characteristics of industry competition can provide practical insights for domestic industrial policymaking and overseas industrial deployment under the framework of the Belt and Road Initiative. Using Porter's Five Forces model as the analytical framework, this study examines the competitive characteristics of China's new materials industry by drawing on publicly available industry reports, existing literature, and online interviews with industry practitioners, given the constraints on obtaining first-hand corporate research samples. The findings indicate that the industry as a whole has high entry barriers, while supplier bargaining power varies significantly across different segments. Buyers and substitutes exert moderate competitive pressure, and the intensity of intra-industry competition differs substantially between low-end and high-end segments. Based on these findings, corresponding industrial policy recommendations are proposed, followed by a discussion of the limitations of this study and directions for future research.

items.title: Anthropometry-Based Human-Centered Design and Material Engineering of a Walking Aid for Children With Cerebral Palsy
items.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a neurological disorder characterized by impaired movement, balance difficulties, abnormal muscle tone, and motor dysfunction resulting from brain damage during early developmental stages of birth. These impairments significantly influence a child’s ability to perform daily activities and lead an independent life. Therefore, providing appropriate assistive mobility devices is essential to enhance mobility, safety, and overall quality of life for children with CP. Walking aids are commonly used rehabilitation devices designed to support movement and promote independence. Many existing walking aids are not designed using anthropometric data representative of the geographical population for which they are intended, which may reduce their ergonomic suitability. This study addresses this limitation by developing a local anthropometric database for Jordanian children with CP aged 1–5 years. Anthropometric measurements were collected and analyzed to support ergonomic design requirements. Based on these measurements, dimensional requirements were established and translated into a conceptual computer-aided design (CAD) of an adjustable walking aid. The proposed conceptual design incorporates appropriate dimensional specifications derived from the collected anthropometric data to ensure comfort, stability, and safety. Jansen mechanism of motion is applied to the new design to promote children mobility. The proposed walking aid is intended to accommodate children with CP within the 1–5-year age group, facilitating improved mobility and supporting their participation in daily activities and rehabilitation programs.

items.title: Applications of HFACS in maritime accident research: a systematic review and bibliometric analysis
items.abstract: The Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) is increasingly used and modified in maritime accident research. This study is a systematic review of the use of HFACS in maritime research. Bibliometric patterns in Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus are investigated. The study used a combination of systematic review, content analysis and bibliometric mapping according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The final datasets of WoS and Scopus included 60 studies each, of which 55 were common to both databases, resulting in a total of 65 unique eligible studies. The results show a recent growth in maritime HFACS research, mainly concentrated in China and Türkiye. HFACS is still in widespread use, but a number of maritime-specific adaptations have been proposed and HFACS has been combined with probabilistic, system-oriented and data-driven methods. Analyzing the ten most-cited and ten database-specific studies identified causal factors at different HFACS levels and mitigation measures addressing operational and organizational issues. The citation-network structures of WoS and Scopus were different, but the frequently occurring keywords and highly cited publications and authors were similar. In general, the results show that maritime HFACS research has progressed beyond accident classification by the use of adapted frameworks and complementary analytical methods.

Legal and accounting professions, which rely on expertise, judgment, confidentiality and compliance, are increasingly exposed to AI technologies, though adoption and perceived impacts may differ between the two fields. This study examines and compares AI adoption and professional transformation among legal and accounting professionals in Mumbai. A quantitative research design using a structured questionnaire will be adopted, with data analysed through descriptive, reliability, correlation and comparative statistical techniques. The study aims to identify similarities, differences and factors influencing AI adoption, providing insights for effective AI training, governance and responsible adoption. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and China’s Cross-Border E-Commerce Development: Threshold Effects and Transmission Mechanisms
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence and search technology is transforming traditional online shopping models, particularly cross-border e-commerce (CBEC), which involves complex customer multi-attribute decision-making with numerous considerations. This study systematically examines the influence of artificial intelligence on the high-quality advancement of CBEC and its underlying mechanisms using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces covering the period 2013–2023. The study found a significant positive correlation between artificial intelligence and cross-border e-commerce. This conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness tests (including removing the interference of pandemic-related data, substituting core explanatory variables, substituting the dependent variable, and lagging explanatory variables by one period). Mechanism analysis indicates that the positive impact of AI on the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce is realized through improvements in logistics capabilities and the unlocking of consumer potential, with mediation effects accounting for 40.27% and 17.02%, respectively. Threshold model results show that the positive impact of AI on the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce exhibits a single threshold effect based on the level of human capital; once human capital exceeds the threshold value, the coefficient further increases. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that AI has the most significant empowering effect on the development of cross-border e-commerce in the eastern regions; however, its impact on the central and western regions is relatively minor. It is worth noting that AI exerts its empowering effect more effectively in regions with high e-commerce procurement activity, whereas the relationship is not significant in regions with low activity.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ITS EFFECTS ON STUDENTS’ READING AND WRITING SKILLS AT THE SECONDARY SCHOOL LEVEL
items.abstract: Although international scholarship on AI in education had expanded rapidly, empirical evidence concerning its relationship with the reading and writing skills of secondary-school students in Pakistan had remained limited. The present study examined the relationship between AI use and the reading and writing performance of male students enrolled in public secondary schools in District Sialkot, Punjab. A quantitative, cross-sectional, correlational research design was adopted. The population comprised male students enrolled in Grades 9 and 10 in government secondary schools, from whom a multistage stratified random sample of 270 students was selected. Data were collected through an AI Use in Learning Questionnaire, a researcher-developed reading comprehension test, and an analytical writing performance test. The study differentiated between productive and substitutive forms of AI use. Productive use involved explanation seeking, guided practice, idea generation, verification, formative feedback, and reflective revision, whereas substitutive use involved outsourcing comprehension and composition, copying AI-generated responses, and accepting machine-generated content without critical evaluation. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, analysis of variance, and hierarchical multiple regression were employed to examine the relationships among the variables. The study provided a contextually grounded framework for understanding AI-supported literacy, assessment integrity, digital inequality, teacher mediation, and responsible technology integration in Pakistani secondary education.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LAW
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence ("AI") is increasingly becoming embedded in activities that were traditionally governed by direct human judgment. Automated systems now assist in recruitment, credit assessment, healthcare, education, content generation, surveillance and public administration. The legal significance of this development lies not merely in the sophistication of the technology but in the possibility that consequential decisions may be produced through systems whose operation is difficult for affected individuals to understand or challenge. This creates questions concerning privacy, equality, discrimination, intellectual property, liability, procedural fairness and the allocation of responsibility among developers, deployers and users. India presently addresses these concerns through a combination of constitutional principles, information-technology legislation, data-protection law, sectoral regulation and policy initiatives rather than through a comprehensive AI statute. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, together with the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, has strengthened India's data-governance architecture, but data protection alone cannot resolve the wider accountability problems created by AI. This article examines the principal legal challenges associated with AI and compares India's developing approach with the European Union's risk-based Artificial Intelligence Act and the United States' standards-oriented approach. It argues that India's future AI governance should preserve a legally traceable chain of responsibility whenever decision-making is delegated to automated systems. Such a framework should combine risk classification, meaningful human oversight, transparency, privacy safeguards, anti-discrimination measures, lifecycle accountability and effective remedies. Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming organizational processes, occupational roles, skill requirements and employee expectations. Although AI has the potential to improve productivity and create new employment opportunities, its increasing use may also generate employee concerns regarding job replacement, skill obsolescence, career continuity and employment security. These concerns are particularly relevant in knowledge-intensive and technology-enabled sectors such as real estate, where artificial intelligence, data analytics, automation, digital platforms and intelligent decision-support systems are increasingly influencing organizational activities. The present study develops and proposes an empirical model examining the relationship between Artificial Intelligence Anxiety (AIA) and Employee Engagement (EE) among employees in the Indian real estate sector. Specifically, the study investigates Perceived Job Insecurity (PJI) as a mediating mechanism and Perceived Organizational Support (POS) as a moderating resource. The theoretical foundation integrates Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) theory, Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and Organizational Support Theory. The proposed model suggests that AI anxiety increases perceived job insecurity, which subsequently reduces employee engagement. Perceived organizational support is expected to weaken the positive relationship between AI anxiety and perceived job insecurity and consequently buffer the negative indirect effect of AI anxiety on employee engagement. Data will be collected using established measurement instruments for AI anxiety, job insecurity, perceived organizational support and employee engagement. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), preferably using SmartPLS, will be employed to assess the measurement and structural models, including mediation, moderation and moderated mediation. The proposed study contributes to the emerging literature on the human consequences of AI by moving beyond technology adoption and productivity perspectives and examining the psychological pathway through which AI- related concerns influence employee engagement.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Early Disease Detection in Healthcare Systems
items.abstract: With delayed access to specialist expertise and subjective interpretation by clinicians and workload limiting the ability to access parts of the pathway, early disease detection is one of the most impactful levers that can be used to improve patient outcomes and reduce the cost of care.Medical image analysis, electronic health records (EHR), genomic data analysis, and analysis of physiological signals are all examples of medical data that can be transformed by artificial intelligence (AI) and especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), as there is no way they could be analyzed at the same scale and speed as would be possible by a human being.In this paper we bring together existing evidence of the use of AI in early detection in oncology, cardiology, neurology, dermatology, ophthalmology and critical care.It discusses the mathematical approaches used for their analysis such as the use of convolutional neural networks for image analysis and recurrent networks for time-series analysis of physiological data, and compares their reported diagnostic performance with that of conventional clinical analyses.The paper also examines real-world challenges to adoption, such as standardization of data, algorithmic bias, regulatory approval processes and clinician acceptance, and proposes some solutions.The results suggest that AI systems perform as well as or better than humans in precisely defined detection tasks but will not automatically translate this to better population health outcomes without attention to data quality, the need to integrate AI systems into workflows, and the need to ensure that everyone has access to them.The paper ends with policy, research and system recommendations for maximizing early detection programmatic value while responsibly scaling these initiatives.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Otolaryngology: Current Status and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Otolaryngology is among the medical specialties most suitable for the application of artificial intelligence (AI), largely due to the wide variety of data generated in daily practice. Otoscopic and endoscopic images, voice recordings, audiological tests, vestibular assessments, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and digital pathology slides provide rich sources of information that can be analyzed using AI-based methods. As a result, AI has emerged as a valuable tool for tasks such as image classification, segmentation, risk prediction, outcome estimation, and optimization of clinical workflows. Despite growing scientific interest, however, many AI studies in otolaryngology remain at the developmental stage and have not yet undergone sufficient clinical validation for routine use. Currently, the most practical applications of AI involve well-defined and repetitive clinical tasks. These include supporting newborn hearing screening programs, predicting cochlear implant outcomes, interpreting otoscopic and nasal endoscopic images, assisting vestibular assessments, analyzing voice recordings for laryngeal disorders, and improving risk stratification in head and neck oncology. In contrast, complex clinical decisions that require comprehensive patient evaluation continue to depend on physician expertise, with AI functioning primarily as a supportive technology rather than an independent decision-maker. The future role of AI in otolaryngology is therefore not to replace clinicians but to enhance decision-making by improving efficiency, consistency, and data utilization. Successful implementation will require not only high diagnostic accuracy but also careful attention to validation, data quality, patient privacy, regulatory oversight, and clinical accountability. Consequently, the major challenge ahead is not the development of new algorithms, but their safe and responsible integration into clinical practice.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Cell-Based Therapies in Retinal Disease
items.abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases, including age-related macular degeneration (AMD), retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and Stargardt disease, represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of people. Cell-based therapies, particularly those leveraging induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) transplantation, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, have emerged as promising treatment modalities that may preserve, replace, or partially restore retinal function. However, these approaches face significant challenges in patient stratification, manufacturing consistency, surgical precision, and long-term outcome monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, is increasingly being integrated across the cell therapy pipeline to address these limitations. This review comprehensively explores the role of AI in enhancing cell-based retinal therapies, spanning disease diagnosis and patient selection, stem cell quality control and differentiation optimization, CRISPR off-target detection, retinal organoid characterization, scalable manufacturing, and post-transplantation monitoring through multimodal retinal imaging. Throughout, we distinguish direct retinal cell-therapy evidence from retinal-adjacent, cross-domain, and conceptual evidence. We also propose an AI-powered end-to-end pipeline that connects patient profiling through gene editing, cell production, and transplantation to longitudinal outcomes tracking (a forward-looking framework that needs to be clinically validated in future). While AI offers powerful tools to enhance efficacy, reproducibility, and personalization, it does not replace the clinical and biological foundations of cell therapy. Critical challenges remain, including data scarcity, algorithmic interpretability, regulatory compliance, and clinical validation. This review concludes that the strategic integration of AI has plausible potential to become supportive infrastructure for scalable and reproducible cell-based treatments for retinal diseases, although its necessity has not been demonstrated and prospective clinical validation is still required, and biological insight and rigorous empirical verification remain fundamental.

The applications of AI playing a significant role in managing different sections of industries, whether it is production section, maintenance section or research section. The allocation of raw materials and finished products is also being taken care with the help of new advanced technologies such as IoT, AI/ML, robotics and automation. This paper is mainly focused on the impact of these new technologies on the management and economies of Indian industries. Focus is made on various sectors such as IT, manufacturing, supply chain management. The study explored the effect of AI and modern technologies on the decision making, sustainability, workers dynamics, resource management, economies variations by considering theoretical frameworks and actual related data available. A keen observation on the issues and limitations of these modern technologies are also examined.
